$comment: x86_64 target descriptor (plan 12 §2.6 ML5 cycle 2 pivot — config-driven targets). Parallels src/dss-config/sources/*.lang.json: a compile target is a config file the LIR substrate reads, NOT C++ code. Adding a new target = drop a new .target.json. Loaded via TargetSchema::loadShipped("x86_64").

target.name: x86_64
target.$isaComment: ★★★ THE INSTRUCTION-SET ARCHITECTURE THIS TARGET EXECUTES (D-ISA-LANGUAGE-BOUND-TO-ARCHITECTURE). The TARGET half of an axis whose LANGUAGE half is the optional top-level `isa` in a `.lang.json`; the engine compares the two DECLARED values for equality and reads no name, no format kind and no machine code. ⚠ IT IS NOT `name`. `name` is this document's IDENTITY — the stem a user types in `--target <name>:<format>` — and keying a build decision on it is the identity branch the agnosticism veto forbids. `isa` is a fact about the HARDWARE that several target documents may legitimately share: the day an `x86_64-v3` target ships it declares THIS SAME VALUE and every language already bound to x86-64 accepts it with NO edit to any language document and no code change. That property is the design's acceptance criterion. ⚠ IT IS NOT THE `machine` CODE EITHER — those are per-FORMAT encodings of the arch (`elf.machine` 62 · `pe.machine` 0x8664 · `macho.cputype` 0x01000007 all name THIS ISA), they live on the format side, and cross_validate_target_format reaches them through a table keyed on the target NAME, so they answer 'do this target and this format agree?' and never 'what does this target execute?'. VALUE: the psABI/uname spelling, which is also this arch's LLVM-triple and ELF-format spelling.
target.$dwarfReturnAddressColumnComment: The CIE's `return_address_register` -- the DWARF column an unwinder reads to find where this frame's return address went, and the other half of the psABI numbering whose per-register half is `registers[].dwarfNumber`. ★ DECLARED, NOT DERIVED, and 16 is NOT A REGISTER -- it is a synthetic column with no hardware counterpart, so no register row could carry it and no derivation could produce it (readelf spells it `r16 (rip)`, but `%rip` is not a register a rule may otherwise name). ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 with binutils 2.42 -- `as + readelf --debug-dump=frames` on a `.cfi_startproc` probe prints `Return address column: 16`; the per-register numbers below were read the same way (each `.cfi_offset <name>` makes GAS itself translate the name, so the table is binutils' own rather than one typed from a document). ⚠ THE LOADER REQUIRES BOTH HALVES TOGETHER: this key without any `dwarfNumber`, or any `dwarfNumber` without this key, is REJECTED at load -- half a numbering loads clean and then makes `.eh_frame` silently never appear, which is the exact shape of D-UNWIND-NO-EH-FRAME-ANY-LANGUAGE-ON-ELF-OR-MACHO.
target.description: x86_64 opcode set + physical register file + SysV AMD64 / Microsoft x64 calling conventions. Cycle 2b: regfile/ABI added. Cycle 3 (instruction selection) expands the opcode set to full c-subset corpus coverage.
target.$reservedFields: The per-opcode minOperands/maxOperands fields are documented in the JSON for completeness but are NOT yet fully enforced by the substrate. Terminator-ness derives from `terminatorKind` (Br/CondBr/Switch/Return/Unreachable; default `none` = non-terminator); the parser's `parseInst` and `LirVerifier` consult it directly. Per-kind successor-count is enforced by `TargetSchemaData::validate()` via the shared `kTargetTerminatorShapes` table.

$defaultAssemblyLanguageComment:
★★★ A NAME, AND ONLY A NAME (D-DRIVER-ASM-DIALECT-SELECTED-BY-TARGET, 2026-08-13). This key answers ONE question — 'when the caller names no source language, which shipped `<stem>.lang.json` spells THIS processor's assembly?' — and the value is a `loadShipped` stem, exactly what `--language` takes. It is the ONLY assembly fact this file carries, and that boundary is load-bearing rather than stylistic.
★★ WHY NOT A BLOCK. An `asmSyntax` block WAS added here once — `registerPrefix: "%"`, `immediatePrefix: "$"`, `commentPrefixes`, and operand order via a per-instruction `destinationOperand` — and it was REVERTED the same day it was written, built and gated green ([[D-CONFIG-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARED-AS-TARGET-VOCABULARY]]). ✔THE DISQUALIFYING MEASUREMENT, taken with gcc on THIS target: AT&T `movq %rsi, (%rdi)` versus Intel (`-masm=intel`) `mov QWORD PTR [rdi], rsi` — one CPU, one compiler, two dialects differing in register sigil, immediate sigil, comment character, OPERAND ORDER, memory-operand form and mnemonic spelling. Every one of those is a function of (target, DIALECT); storing them per-target stores a per-(X,Y) fact per-X, and it only looked right because exactly one dialect per target exists today. What is genuinely per-target is WHICH dialect document is the default — this key. Do not re-propose the block.
★ NOT A LIST, DELIBERATELY. `asm-x86_64-intel` is the sibling that would make it one, and it does not exist yet; a list would need a selector, and the only honest selector before a second dialect ships is the one that already works — naming the language explicitly (`--language asm-x86_64-intel`). A `-masm=`-style flag today would be a knob with nothing to switch to.
★ OMITTING THIS KEY IS A LEGITIMATE STATE, not a malformed document: a target with no assembly dialect simply fails loud BY NAME when a build needs one. The empty string is REJECTED by the loader, because 'absent' and 'meant to fill this in' are operator-distinguishable and folding them together is how a config key stops meaning anything.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C74: the per-ARCHITECTURE identity macros this CPU predefines, merged with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` at preprocess time. Declared on the TARGET (like aggregateLayout/tls below) because they are per-CPU facts; putting them on the language would force c-subset.lang.json to enumerate CPU architectures. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by BOTH this file and the language config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) — neither side silently wins. GATING (MEASURED 2026-07-28 with `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>`): all four spellings are defined identically by x86_64-linux-gnu, x86_64-apple-darwin AND x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, so all four are UNGATED — unlike the arm64 twin, where `__arm64__`/`__arm64` are Apple-only and must carry availableObjectFormats. DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: `_M_X64` (an MSVC TOOLCHAIN-profile macro, not a CPU fact — it belongs with the pe-gated `_MSC_VER` family on the language side); SHIPPED, BUT NOT HERE -- LANDED ON THE OBJECT FORMAT (TF-C97, D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): `__LP64__`/`_LP64` are a DATA MODEL, not an architecture -- x86_64:pe64 is LLP64 while the SAME CPU is LP64 under elf64/macho64 -- so a row here would be wrong on one of this target's own formats. This note used to read 'DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED' and was a HANDOFF that went four cycles uncompleted; it is now DONE: every LP64 `*.format.json` declares both spellings through the format schema's own `predefinedMacros` key (the same key name, the same shared entry grammar, the same C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro collision policy as this file's), and every LLP64/ILP32 one declares NEITHER -- the negative being the whole reason the channel sits at the format layer. Do not add them here. ★ `__BYTE_ORDER__` USED TO BE LISTED HERE AS 'DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED (its value must be a macro REFERENCE, e.g. `__ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__`, which needs a different mechanism than a literal Constant body)'. THAT CLAIM WAS FALSE AND IS NOW REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT (TF-C115, D-PP-ENDIANNESS-PREDEFINES): the `constant` kind ALREADY carries a macro-reference body, because a materialized predefine is spliced over its invocation and RESCANNED like any other replacement (`preprocessor.cpp` — `spliceOver(...); continue;   // rescan from the materialized value`). MEASURED 2026-08-04 against a patched config copy reached through DSS_CONFIG_ROOT: with `__BYTE_ORDER__` = `__ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__`, all of `defined(__BYTE_ORDER__)`, `__BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__`, `__BYTE_ORDER__ == 1234` and `!(__BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__)` hold; the same probe against the UNPATCHED config fired 6 of its 8 `#error` legs (A/B/C/E/F/G; 6 x P001E), INCLUDING the one asserting `__BYTE_ORDER__ != __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` — i.e. the unshipped state was not merely silent, it selected the BIG-ENDIAN arm of any such ladder (`0 == 0`, C 6.10.1p4). No engine change was needed; the note had never been tested. The two endianness rows are now SHIPPED below. Still DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: toolchain identity (`__GNUC__`/`__clang__`) which is a COMPILER profile, not a CPU.
$endiannessPredefinesComment: TF-C115 (D-PP-ENDIANNESS-PREDEFINES). ★ THIS IS A DOCUMENTATION KEY ONLY — there is deliberately NO `endianness` root key (see below); it annotates the two endianness rows in `predefinedMacros`. THE LAYER, ARGUED FROM THE SAME RULE `__LP64__` LOST ON: a fact belongs on the layer where it does not vary. Endianness DOES vary by CPU (MEASURED: clang defines `__BIG_ENDIAN__` and `__BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` for aarch64_be-linux-gnu, `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` for aarch64-linux-gnu) and does NOT vary across the object formats a single DSS target serves — x86_64 is little-endian under elf64, macho64 AND pe64, and arm64 is little-endian under elf64 and macho64 — which is precisely the test `__LP64__` FAILED (x86_64 is LP64 on elf/macho and LLP64 on pe, so its row had to move to the format). So these belong HERE, per-CPU, exactly like `__x86_64__`. NO SEPARATE `endianness` KEY IS DECLARED alongside them: the `charIsUnsigned` precedent (arm64.target.json) shows that a second notation of one fact is a DRIFT SOURCE requiring its own coherence test, and unlike `charIsUnsigned` — which HIR→MIR genuinely reads for the char→int promotion — nothing in the engine consumes an endianness value today (`bitFieldStrategy` already carries the LSB-first bit-field rule these targets need). A key with no consumer is dead config that can silently disagree with the macro; the day a consumer exists, it gets declared and THEN gets its coherence example. GATING (MEASURED 2026-08-04, `clang-19 -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>`, Ubuntu clang 19.1.1): `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` is defined as 1 on ALL FIVE little-endian triples DSS targets — arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu AND x86_64-pc-windows-msvc — so it is UNGATED, like the four x86_64 identity spellings above and unlike arm64's Apple-only `__arm64__`. Same for `__BYTE_ORDER__`. ★ `__BIG_ENDIAN__` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECLARATION: MEASURED, clang defines it ONLY on a big-endian triple (aarch64_be-linux-gnu), so shipping it anywhere here would be a lie about the machine, and Apple's `libkern/OSByteOrder.h` selects its swap-macro family on `defined(__BIG_ENDIAN__)` FIRST — a stray row would silently pick byte-swapping macros on a little-endian host. The negative is asserted by examples/c-subset/endianness_predefines, which is red if `__BIG_ENDIAN__` ever appears on any leg. ★ NOT A GCC PROFILE: MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 (native x86_64 and the aarch64-linux-gnu cross) defines `__BYTE_ORDER__` and the `__ORDER_*` triple but NOT `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` — that spelling is a clang/Apple-toolchain one. Shipping it is consistent with the identity this compiler already claims unconditionally (`__clang__` in c-subset.lang.json), and it is what unblocks the Apple SDK: `libkern/OSByteOrder.h:314` is a bare `#error Unknown endianess.` when neither spelling is defined. THE `__ORDER_*` CONSTANTS THIS ROW'S VALUE NAMES ARE NOT HERE — they are invariant across every triple and live on the LANGUAGE (c-subset.lang.json); see that row's comment for the argument.
$aggregateLayoutComment: FC6 (D-FF3-1): per-ABI struct/union/array layout params the generic type_layout engine reads. `natural` = scalar alignment equals its byte size (capped at maxAlignment) — the rule all four current C ABIs (SysV/Win64/AAPCS64/Apple) share; the format's dataModel supplies the OS-dependent pointer width. maxAlignment 16 = the x86_64 max fundamental alignment (__int128/long double/max_align_t). D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: `bitFieldStrategy` here is the BACK-COMPAT FALLBACK only — C bit-field packing is OS/format-determined (this CPU serves BOTH ELF-SysV gnu_packed AND PE-MS msvc_straddle), so the ACTIVE strategy is resolved from the object FORMAT (effectiveBitFieldStrategy). The fallback is used only by direct-API / test callers with no format in scope.
$tlsComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the CPU's static-TLS layout convention — psABI-per-CPU data (x86_64 is Variant II under EVERY OS, so it lives on the TARGET, not the format). variant2 = the thread pointer points ONE PAST the TLS block's end (fs:[0] holds tp itself); a symbol's link-time thread-pointer offset is NEGATIVE: tpoff = templateOffset − alignUp(blockSize, p_align). tcbHeaderBytes = 0 (a Variant-I-only input — arm64 declares 16 with its own block at TLS C2). Consumed ONLY by the walker's tpoff helper when the format's tlsAccess.model is local-exec — a config-keyed formula selector, never a machine-identity branch.

opcodes.$comment: Slot 0 = the Invalid sentinel. Every target must declare it as the first opcode so the substrate's `opcode == 0` check (in LirBuilder::addInst) catches default-constructed insts loudly.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op: 'this LirReg is the function's k-th input parameter' (payload = k). ML7 calling-convention lowering rewrites `arg` to the real mov-from-arg-register sequence; before that, it represents the parameter as a virtreg that ML5 cycle 3 MIR→LIR isel can consume directly. Every target backend needs SOME representation of 'i-th function parameter'; pre-regalloc this is the uniform shape.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC7 C1c, D-FC7-SYSV-STRUCT-RETURN-IN-REGS): 'this LirReg is the k-th return register of the immediately-preceding struct-returning call' (payload = per-class return-register ordinal). The caller-side mirror of `arg`. ML7 calling-convention lowering captures it (a mov-from-returnReg, cycle-broken with its sibling pieces) and the ret_piece itself is never encoded. side-effecting so no pass drops/hoists it off its call.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC7 C3) — callee-side mirror of `arg`: 'this LirReg is the incoming indirect-result (sret) pointer', read from the cc's indirectResultRegister at function entry. Declared for substrate uniformity (like `ret_piece`); x86_64's SysV/ms_x64 conventions pass the sret pointer as a HIDDEN ARG (no indirectResultRegister), so this op is never EMITTED on x86_64 — only register-based sret (AAPCS64/Apple x8) emits it. No encoding (materialized away by lir_callconv).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC12a-core, D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): 'this LirReg is the ADDRESS of the variadic register-save-area' — the frame zone a variadic callee's prologue spills rdi..r9 + the al-gated xmm0..7 into. lir_callconv reserves the zone (sized by the cc's vaListLayout.regSaveAreaBytes) + materializes this op into `lea result, [sp + offset]` once the frame layout is known. The PRESENCE of this op in a function is also lir_callconv's signal that the function called va_start (→ emit the spill). No encoding (materialized away).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC12a-core, D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): 'this LirReg is the ADDRESS of the incoming overflow stack args' — where varargs that didn't fit in registers live (the caller's outgoing-args area, above this frame). lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [sp + totalFrameSize + callPushBytes + shadowSpaceBytes]` (the same geometry the stack-resident `arg` read uses; on SysV shadowSpaceBytes=0 so it is `totalFrameSize + callPushBytes`). NOTE (FC12b): this offset's `totalFrameSize + callPushBytes` base ALSO serves as the Win64 va_home_arg_area home base, which must NOT include shadowSpaceBytes — the Win64 home leaf is a SEPARATE op (`va_home_arg_area`) so this op may keep its shadow term; do not collapse them. No encoding (materialized away).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS): callee-side mirror of the caller's `ByValueStackArg` carrier — 'this LirReg is the ADDRESS of a FIXED by-value aggregate param that was placed WHOLLY on the incoming stack' (it straddled the reg/stack boundary, all-or-nothing). lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [sp + totalFrameSize + callPushBytes + shadowSpaceBytes + payload]` — IDENTICAL geometry to va_overflow_arg_area but the PAYLOAD is THIS aggregate's byte offset WITHIN the incoming overflow area (0 when it is the first/only overflowed fixed param). HIR→MIR then byte-copies from this address into the param's local slot. DISTINCT from the va_* ops on purpose: it must NOT be one of lir_callconv's va_start-detection signals (it occurs in NON-variadic functions too — reusing va_overflow_arg_area would falsely trigger the variadic prologue spill). No encoding (materialized away).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (c69, D-CSUBSET-ALLOCA-ADDRESS-REMATERIALIZE): a RE-REFERENCE of a body-local's stack slot — 'this fresh LirReg is the ADDRESS of local-alloca #k', where k = PAYLOAD = the alloca's 0-based scan-order index within the function. The c69 entry-block alloca-hoist makes every local's address live from function entry; reusing ONE address vreg across that range tips a register-pressure cliff, so MIR->LIR emits the `alloca` op ONCE (it reserves the slot) and a fresh `lea_frame_slot k` at EACH use of the address — each result has a tiny def->use range, the conventional 'rematerialize frame addresses' treatment. lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [sp + localAreaOffset + offsetOf(k) + disp]` — byte-identical to the `lea` the original alloca (same k) resolves to (offset read from the alloca-index->offset map lir_callconv builds in scan order). An OPTIONAL single ImmInt operand is a folded CONSTANT byte displacement `disp` (a `&local[constIdx]`/`&s.field` Gep whose base IS this alloca, folded by lowerGep into ONE sp-based frame lea) — this is cheaper (one lea) AND keeps the arm64 >16 MiB MOVZ/MOVK lea macro safe (base = sp, never the result reg, so `MOVZ Xd;ADD Xd,sp,Xd` never clobbers the base). DISTINCT from `alloca` so it is INVISIBLE to the frame-layout slot-count scan (`functionLocalAllocaPayloads` counts only `alloca`): the frame still reserves exactly ONE slot per original alloca. No encoding (materialized away). hasSideEffects=false (a pure address computation, like `lea`/`alloca`); no LIR-tier pass removes/merges it (the pipeline runs no LIR DCE/CSE), so its result-used ranges always survive to materialization.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (c116 H1, D-WIN64-SEH-FUNCLETS): 'this fresh LirReg is the ADDRESS of local-slot #k IN THE FRAME the operand[0] register establishes' — the generic analog of LLVM's llvm.localrecover. operand[0] = an establisher-frame base pointer register; PAYLOAD = k = the 0-based scan-order index of a local in that frame. lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [establisherReg + parentLocalAreaOffset(k)]`, where parentLocalAreaOffset comes from the config FrameLayout of the frame the base establishes (the SAME localAreaOffset()+k*slotSize geometry `alloca`/`lea_frame_slot` use, but based off the establisher REGISTER rather than SP, and against the PARENT function's finalized layout — lir_callconv threads sibling layouts + the funclet->parent map to resolve it). The c116 SEH filter FUNCLET is its first consumer: a __except filter reading a parent local (sqlite's `pWal`) recovers it via `[establisher + parentSlotOffset]`, since a fault-time x64 establisher frame (FrameRegister=0) == the parent's post-prologue SP. AGNOSTIC: base is a normal SSA operand (never a hardcoded rdx), the offset is from FrameLayout, and the op names nothing arch/format/SEH-specific. No encoding (materialized away). hasSideEffects=false (a pure address computation, like `lea`/`alloca`/`lea_frame_slot`).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC12b, D-FC12B-WIN64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): 'this LirReg is the ADDRESS of the Win64 HomogeneousPointer va_start base' — &home[namedArgCount], the first vararg. Win64's named-arg home space (rcx/rdx/r8/r9 slots) and the 5th+ stack args are CONTIGUOUS in the caller's outgoing area, so this single base + the named-arg slot count positions `ap` past ALL named args. PAYLOAD = the named-arg slot count; lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [sp + totalFrameSize + callPushBytes + payload*outgoingSlotSize]` — the NO-SHADOW base (the home space IS the caller's shadow space, so adding shadowSpaceBytes would skip it and read past every named arg). Its PRESENCE is also lir_callconv's signal to spill the named integer arg regs into their home slots. No encoding (materialized away).

2-operand-shape mov: destination = result vreg, source = operands[0]. AS2 cycle 2 wires this to two encoding variants: REX.W 0x8B /r (mov r64, r64) when source is a register; REX.W 0xC7 /0 imm32 (mov r/m64, imm32 SIGN-extended to 64-bit) when source is an immediate. FC3 c2 (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS): both shapes gain explicit `width` keys + 32-bit siblings (same opcodes WITHOUT REX.W, Intel SDM Vol. 2B MOV) — a 32-bit register write auto-zero-extends to the full 64-bit register, and the 32-bit imm32 form is EXACT (not sign-extending), the difference that matters for an `unsigned int` 0xFFFFFFFF. Plumbing movs (phi/copy/capture/spill) are emitted width-default (64) — full-register copies are value-correct for every type. FC8 (D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-WIDE-UNIT): a fifth variant materializes a FULL 64-bit immediate — REX.W B8+rd io (mov r64, imm64) — selected by the `imm64` operand-kind (a `LiteralIndex` LIR operand: the wide value lives in the LIR literal pool, since it does not fit the inline imm32 path). This is the ONLY x86-64 form that loads a >imm32 constant into a register; its destination rides the opcode byte (B8+rd), not ModR/M, so it uses the `opcode.reg` result slot.

variants.$comment: mov r32, r32 — 0x8B /r without REX.W (zero-extends to r64).

★★★ mov r16, r16 — 0x66 0x8B /r (D-ASM-SUB-NATIVE-OPERAND-UNUSABLE-IN-INLINE-ASM, 2026-08-23). The 0x66 operand-size prefix selects the 16-bit form and MUST precede any REX (the walker's mandatoryPrefix step runs before its REX step, which is exactly this ordering rule). Writes ONLY bits 15:0 of the destination — the upper 48 bits are LEFT UNCHANGED, which is what distinguishes a 16-bit MOV from the zero-extending MOVZX the `load` rows use, and why a `short` inline-asm operand needs this row rather than a wider one. First consumer: the AT&T dialect's `movw` spelling, whose only C-side reachable shape is a `short`-typed `"r"` operand.

★★★ mov r8, r/m8 — 0x8A /r (D-ASM-SUB-NATIVE-OPERAND-UNUSABLE-IN-INLINE-ASM, 2026-08-23). Writes ONLY bits 7:0; the upper 56 are left unchanged. ⚠⚠ `forceRexPrefix: true` IS A CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT, NOT A SIZE CHOICE, and it is the same rule `setcc` and `store`'s byte row already carry: WITHOUT a REX prefix, byte-register encodings 4..7 name the LEGACY HIGH bytes `ah`/`ch`/`dh`/`bh` instead of `spl`/`bpl`/`sil`/`dil` — i.e. a DIFFERENT physical register, silently. A template operand binds whichever GPR the allocator chose, so all 16 must be reachable.
mov r/m32, imm32 — 0xC7 /0 without REX.W: writes the EXACT 32-bit immediate + zero upper (the 64-bit form sign-extends).

mov r/m8, imm8 — 0xC6 /0 ib (2026-08-23, the `movb $5, %al` spelling). The `imm32` operand KIND is the JSON-side label for `OperandKindFilter::ImmInt`; the SLOT is what decides how many bytes are emitted, and `imm8` emits one — the same pairing the shift rows use for their `ib` count. `forceRexPrefix` for the byte-register rationale on the row above. ⚠⚠ THIS SENTENCE SHIPPED FALSE AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE RATHER THAN DELETED, BECAUSE THE SHAPE IS THE REUSABLE PART — AND IT IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE IN THE TREE: it said THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO 16-BIT SIBLING and that the spelling STAYS FAIL-LOUD, and the 16-bit sibling it denies sits FOURTEEN LINES BELOW IT IN THIS SAME FILE, added by the same commit. The reason it gave was real up to that moment: `movw $5, %ax` is `0x66 0xC7 /0 iw` — a TWO-byte immediate — and the x86-variable walker declared no 2-byte immediate slot, so declaring the row with an `imm32` slot would have emitted FOUR bytes where the instruction takes two, i.e. a corrupt instruction stream with no diagnostic. That is why the spelling was fail-loud rather than approximated, and it is still why an `imm32` slot must never be substituted here. The slot now exists as `EncodingSlotKind::Imm16Bytes` (the older `Imm16` belongs to the fixed32 shape and `checkSlotShape` still refuses THAT one here at load), the width-16 row below wires it, and [[D-ASM-X86-NO-16BIT-IMMEDIATE-SLOT]] is CLOSED. ⇒ a cross-lane citation of an OPEN row is a claim with an expiry date, and the fold is when it expires ([[D-COMMENT-A-CLAIM-TRUE-WHEN-TYPED-AND-FALSE-WHEN-THE-COMMIT-LANDED]]).

FC8 (D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-WIDE-UNIT): mov r64, imm64 — REX.W (0x48) + B8+rd + 8-byte LE immediate (Intel SDM Vol. 2B MOV, REX.W B8+rd io). The destination register's low 3 bits ride the opcode byte (B8+rd) via the `opcode.reg` result slot; its high bit drives REX.B. The `imm64` operand-kind is a `LirOperand{kind==LiteralIndex}` — the wide value lives in the LIR literal pool (the 8-byte operand POD cannot inline a 64-bit immediate), and the encoder reads it back to emit the 8 LE bytes of the `io` field. width:64 keys it to 64-bit constants only; there is no 32-bit imm64 form (a 32-bit-typed wide constant uses the imm32 forms above).

★★★ THE ROW THIS ANCHOR IS NAMED FOR — D-ASM-X86-NO-16BIT-IMMEDIATE-SLOT. `movw $42, %cx` = 0x66 0xC7 /0 iw, a TWO-byte immediate. The previous cycle declared the byte sibling (0xC6 /0 ib) and had to leave this one refused because the x86-variable walker had no 2-byte immediate slot; `imm16.bytes` is that slot. ⚠ NOT byte-identical to gas, which prefers the accumulator/+rw short form `0x66 0xB9 iw` (4 bytes vs 5) — the same deliberate difference the byte and 32-bit rows already carry for register-DIRECT immediates; both encode the same instruction. ✔MEASURED against GNU as 2.42: `movw $42, %cx`.

opcodes.$comment:
add reg-reg — REX.W 0x01 /r (ADD r/m64, r64). LIR is 3-address (dst, src1, src2); requires2Address=true makes the legalize pass insert `mov dst, src1` first when dst!=src1, then the assembler emits `add dst, src2` (writing into ModR/M.rm, which is dst).

★ `requires2Address: true` MEANS *result == operand[0]*, AND THE OPERAND IS NOW NAMEABLE (D-LIR-TIED-OPERAND-NOT-EXPRESSIBLE, 2026-08-15). A sibling key `twoAddressSourceOperand: <j>` ties the result to operand j instead; omitted, it is 0, which is what every opcode in this document and in arm64.target.json means today. The index is a SEPARATE key on purpose: `requires2Address: 1` would read to a human as "true" and to the loader as "tie to operand 1", so the polymorphic spelling was rejected. The loader refuses the index without the flag, refuses an index >= maxOperands, and refuses a non-integer. ⚠ Two rules move WITH the index and both are enforced at load: the tied operand's `guard.operandKinds[j]` must be `reg` (the legalize pass copies FROM it, and it cannot copy from an immediate — which is why `add`/`sub` could not be re-tied to operand 1 at all, their imm32 variants forbid it), and the variant's destination wire must sit on operand j (after legalize THAT operand is the destination).

★★★ THE MEMORY-DESTINATION ARITHMETIC FAMILY — `add_mem` / `sub_mem` / `and_mem` / `or_mem` / `xor_mem` / `not_mem` / `neg_mem` (D-TARGET-X86-64-DECLARES-NO-MEMORY-DESTINATION-ARITHMETIC, 2026-08-23). ONE $comment for seven rows because they differ only in an opcode byte and a ModR/M digit; each row below carries its own pair.
★★★ WHY THEY ARE SEPARATE OPCODES RATHER THAN VARIANTS ON `add`/`sub`/… , AND IT IS THE ENGINE'S RULE RATHER THAN A STYLE CHOICE: `AsmInstructionLowering::buildLirInst` splits a row's candidate opcodes into PRODUCERS (`result: value`) and CONSUMERS (`result: none`) and offers a MEMORY-DESTINATION operand list to the consumers ONLY. `add` produces a value, so no variant of it can ever be elected for `addq $5, -16(%rbp)`. This is the SAME split one mnemonic already has: AT&T `movq` is `mov` (reg→reg), `load` (mem→reg) and `store` (reg→mem) — three opcodes behind one spelling, chosen by which operand is memory.
★★★ AND THE SPLIT IS ALSO WHAT KEEPS THE TWO DIRECTIONS FROM COLLIDING, WHICH IS A SILENT-MISCOMPILE GUARD RATHER THAN TIDINESS. ✔MEASURED by reading the lowering: the memory-DESTINATION list for `subq %rax, mem` is `[reg, reg, MemBase, MemOffset]` and the memory-SOURCE list for `subq mem, %rax` is `[reg, reg, MemBase, MemOffset]` — BYTE-IDENTICAL guards for `mem := mem - rax` (0x29 /r) and `rax := rax - mem` (0x2B /r), two different instructions with OPPOSITE operands. They stay distinguishable only because they live on two opcodes that are elected from two disjoint candidate sets: shape 3 (memory destination) reaches the `*_mem` consumers, shape 1 (register destination) reaches the producers, and shape 2 is withheld outright while a memory operand is present AND the row lists a producer.
⚠ THE ONE MNEMONIC THAT CANNOT TAKE THIS TREATMENT IS `cmp`, AND IT IS ANCHORED RATHER THAN GUESSED AT: `cmp` is ALREADY `result: none`, so its row lists NO producer, shape 2 is therefore offered, and the two byte-identical lists above would both reach the same candidate set — the collision this family avoids by construction. `cmpq` against memory stays fail-loud (`A0008`) in both directions. See [[D-ASM-X86-CMP-AGAINST-MEMORY-DIRECTION-IS-UNELECTABLE]].
★ `result: none` + `hasSideEffects: true` — these write MEMORY, exactly like `store`, so no pass may drop or reorder them. `requires2Address` is deliberately ABSENT: the schema loader refuses it on a `result: none` opcode (there is no destination register to legalize into), and there is nothing to legalize — the destination IS the memory operand the wires name.

opcodes.$comment:
★★ THREE-OPERAND IMUL WITH AN IMMEDIATE — `imul $imm, src, dst` (`69 /r id` and `66 69 /r iw`). D-ASM-X86-IMUL-IMMEDIATE-FORM-UNDECLARED. ✔MEASURED at the CLI before this opcode existed: `imulq $300, %rcx, %rdx` and even the two-operand shorthand `imulq $300, %rax` were refused with `error[A0008] … no candidate target opcode encodes that shape`, at every width — `mul` declares only register and memory-source forms. gas 2.42 assembles all six spellings and gcc emits them for a multiply by a constant.
★★★ WHY A SECOND OPCODE RATHER THAN VARIANTS ON `mul`, and it is not bookkeeping: `mul` is `requires2Address: true` — its destination IS its first operand, which is what the 2-address legalizer guarantees and what its variants' `modrm.reg` wire depends on. The three-operand form writes a destination that is NEITHER source, so it declares a `resultSlot` and no 2-address requirement. One opcode cannot be both, and declaring the immediate variants on `mul` would have handed the legalizer an instruction whose operand 0 is an IMMEDIATE.
⚠ BOTH WRITTEN SHAPES REACH IT, THROUGH THE ENGINE'S EXISTING TWO-ADDRESS RETRY: `imulq $300, %rcx, %rdx` builds `[imm32, reg]` and elects the 3-operand guard directly; the shorthand `imulq $300, %rax` builds `[imm32]`, matches nothing, and the retry prepends the destination to give `[reg, imm32]` — the second guard — which encodes `imul rax, rax, imm`, exactly what gas emits for it. ⚠ NOT byte-identical to gas for a SMALL immediate: gas contracts to the sign-extended `6B /r ib` short form when the value fits a byte, and these rows always emit the long form. Same instruction, one extra immediate byte — the same deliberate difference the register-direct `mov`/ALU immediate rows already carry.

The two-operand SHORTHAND, width 64: `imulq $300, %rax`, which gas expands to `imul dst, dst, imm`. Reached through the engine's two-address retry, which prepends the written destination — so operand 0 is the multiplicand AND the result. ✔MEASURED against GNU as 2.42.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): `sub_sp_reg sp, <sizeReg>` — subtract a RUNTIME byte count (in a register) from the stack pointer, the dynamic-alloca core (`int a[n]` => `sub rsp, alignUp(n*4,16)`). REX.W 0x29 /r (SUB r/m64, r64), the SAME opcode as `sub` reg-reg but a DISTINCT mnemonic (its own single encoding: operand0=sp is BOTH the r/m destination AND source1, operand1=size is the r64 source2). result:none (SP mutates in place — no SSA value; the moved SP is captured by a following `sp_copy`). hasSideEffects=true so no pass drops/reorders it relative to the sp_copy that captures the result. Emitted by MIR->LIR (with the physical stack-pointer operand); the callconv pass passes it through unchanged.

D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): `sp_copy dst, src` — a plain register move used for the three frame-pointer plumbing roles a VLA function needs: prologue FP<-SP (capture the fixed-frame base), epilogue SP<-FP (discard the VLA + restore SP to the fixed-frame base), and the VLA-base capture base<-SP (the post-`sub_sp_reg` stack pointer). REX.W 0x8B /r (MOV r64, r/m64), a DISTINCT mnemonic from `mov` so it can be marked hasSideEffects=true (it reads/writes the physical SP; no pass may drop or reorder it across the `sub_sp_reg`). resultSlot modrm.reg = dst; operand0=src -> modrm.rm. rsp/rbp are valid register-direct in both fields.

D-CSUBSET-VLA (C5): `sp_restore sp, <savedReg>` = `mov rsp, savedReg` — RESTORE the stack pointer to a previously-captured watermark (a StackSave's `sp_copy`), the block-scope VLA teardown emitted on every NON-return exit of a VLA-declaring scope (fall-through / loop back-edge / break / continue / goto). REX.W 0x89 /r (MOV r/m64, r64): operand0=sp is the r/m DESTINATION (modrm.rm), operand1=saved is the r64 SOURCE (modrm.reg). A DISTINCT mnemonic + result:none (SP mutates in place, NOT an SSA value) — mirrors `sub_sp_reg` keeping SP an operand, NEVER the `sp_copy`-with-SP-as-result shape (audit fix #5). hasSideEffects=true so no pass drops/reorders it vs the sub_sp_reg / sp_copy around it. Emitted by MIR->LIR with the physical stack-pointer operand; the callconv passes it through unchanged.

D-WIN64-LARGE-FRAME-STACK-PROBE: a SINGLE LIR op that the x86_64 encoder lowers to a MULTI-INSTRUCTION inline stack-probe loop (one-LIR-op→N-instructions). Operands: [sp(reg), frameBytes(imm32), pageBytes(imm32)] — the stack-pointer register, the total frame size to descend, and the guard-page step (= the cc's stackProbePageBytes). The ML7 prologue emits this INSTEAD of a bare `sub rsp, F` when totalFrameSize > stackProbePageBytes, so the loop touches (commits) every guard page on the way down (Windows reserves the stack lazily behind a single PAGE_GUARD page; a bare `sub` skips it → access violation). The encoder hand-pushes the loop: `mov r11d, frame` / .L: `sub rsp, page` / `or qword [rsp], 0` (page-touch) / `sub r11d, page` / `cmp r11d, page` / `ja .L` (rel8 back) / `sub rsp, r11` (final remainder). r11 is ms_x64 caller-saved, never an arg/return reg, and the probe runs before any arg-home, so it is free. NO __chkstk, NO relocation (the rel8 is a compile-time constant). This is x86_64-ONLY: arm64 OMITS this opcode entirely (its CCs have stackProbePageBytes=0 → never emitted → arm64 encoder would fire A_NoEncodingDeclared, defense-in-depth). The encoding block below exists ONLY to satisfy the shape/routing contract (shape!=None ⇒ asm.cpp routes to the x86-variable walker; the walker's DEDICATED stack_probe arm intercepts BEFORE variant matching and hand-emits the bytes — the variant row itself is never consumed for emission). hasSideEffects=true so no pass drops/reorders it.

variants.$comment: Contract-only variant (see opcode $comment): the x86-variable walker's DEDICATED stack_probe arm emits the probe loop by hand BEFORE this variant is ever matched, so this row carries NO operand wiring (an empty guard — the schema's per-position wire check requires a wire for every declared operandKind, but the probe op's 3 operands are consumed by the hand-written arm, not by slot wiring). Its sole purpose is to make `encoding.shape != None` so asm.cpp routes stack_probe to the x86-variable walker (and opcodeInfo != nullptr, avoiding A_NoEncodingDeclared). If the dedicated arm ever fails to intercept (mnemonic drift), this empty-guard variant does NOT match the 3-operand inst -> A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant fires LOUD (never a silent mis-encode). `template.opcode` is a placeholder never emitted.

opcodes.$comment: 2-operand multiply. x86 has both 2-op `imul reg, reg` (writes the low half to the destination — what we emit) and 1-op `mul/imul reg` (rdx:rax full-width — needed only for overflow/128-bit results, future cycle). The 2-op form is REX.W 0x0F 0xAF /r — UNUSUAL among x86 binary arith because dest goes to ModR/M.reg (not r/m), source-1 goes to r/m. Wires reflect this: op[0]→modrm.reg (the destination per 2-address), op[1]→modrm.rm.

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: imul r32, r/m32 — 0F AF /r without REX.W (32-bit multiply, low half, zero-extends; the C-defined unsigned-int product mod 2^32).

imul r64, [base + disp32] — REX.W 0F AF /r. ★ THE MEMORY-SOURCE FORM IS THE ONLY MEMORY FORM THIS MNEMONIC HAS, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: ✔GNU as 2.42 REJECTS `imulq %rax, -16(%rbp)` and `imulq $5, -16(%rbp)` — the two-operand IMUL writes a REGISTER, so there is no memory-destination `imul` to declare and no `mul_mem` sibling exists. Since 0F AF /r ALREADY places its destination in ModR/M.reg, the memory rows differ from the register rows only in the second operand's slot.
imul r32, [base + disp32] — 0F AF /r without REX.W.

`imulw %ax, %cx` — 0x66 0x0F 0xAF /r. ⚠ THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO WIDTH-8 SIBLING AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OMISSION: ✔GNU as 2.42 REJECTS `imulb %al, %cl` — x86 has no two-operand byte IMUL (only the one-operand AL form), so declaring one would accept input no reference assembler takes. ✔MEASURED against GNU as 2.42: `imulw %ax, %cx`.
`imulw 4096(%r15), %ax` — the width-16 memory-source form. ✔MEASURED against GNU as 2.42: `imulw 4096(%r15), %ax`.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-DIVISION-OP-CODEGEN — CQO sign-extend (cycle 10r split, 2026-06-04). Sign-extends RAX into RDX:RAX as the pre-divide setup for signed division. REX.W 0x99 = 0x48 0x99 (2 bytes, no ModR/M). **Cycle 10r REX-overlap bug fix**: cycle 10q packaged CQO+IDIV as a single compound opcode with `opcode: [72, 153, 72, 247]`. But the encoder auto-emits one REX prefix at the start (e.g., 0x41 for REX.B when the operand is R14) — per x86 decode the LAST REX prefix before the opcode wins, so the embedded literal second 0x48 (REX.W only) superseded the auto-REX 0x41, losing REX.B for the IDIV operand. Result: IDIV reads `modrm.rm low 3 bits` as RSI (without REX.B) instead of R14, dividing by garbage — STATUS_INTEGER_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO trap. Splitting CQO into its own opcode lets each instruction get its own auto-REX correctly. implicitRegisters: inputs=[rax] (CQO reads RAX); outputs=[rdx] (CQO writes the sign-extended high half); clobbered=[rdx] (RDX's prior value is destroyed).

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: the 32-bit sibling is CDQ — the SAME 0x99 opcode WITHOUT REX.W (Intel SDM CWD/CDQ/CQO: operand size selects which) — sign-extends EAX into EDX:EAX, the pre-divide setup the 32-bit IDIV consumes. The MIR→LIR div lowering threads ONE width through the pre+core pair so they always agree.

opcodes.$comment:
No-operation. ✔MEASURED (gcc 13.3.0, `gcc -c` + objdump on a `.s` containing a bare `nop`): ONE byte, 0x90, no ModR/M, no REX, no operands. The x86 encoder auto-emits REX only when an operand demands it, and this form has none.
★ `hasSideEffects: true` IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD, not decoration. A `nop` produces no result (`result: none`), so a pure declaration would make it dead by definition and a dead-code pass would be RIGHT to delete it — deleting the one instruction whose entire purpose is to occupy bytes (alignment padding, a patch point, an `__asm__("nop")` the programmer wrote on purpose). ⚠ HONEST SCOPE OF THAT CLAIM: today's CSE/DCE/LICM read the MIR-tier flag (`src/opt/passes/{cse.cpp:84,dce.cpp:52,licm.cpp:93}`), not this LIR-tier one, so `true` here is a correct DECLARATION rather than a currently-live guard — and it is the value that stays correct when a LIR-tier DCE lands.

Read Time-Stamp Counter. ✔MEASURED (gcc 13.3.0, objdump): `0f 31`, TWO bytes, no ModR/M, no operands — and NO REX.W, because RDTSC always writes EDX:EAX regardless of operand size (a REX.W form does not exist). sqlite's own `hwtime.h` is the client: `__asm__ volatile("rdtsc" : "=a"(lo), "=d"(hi))`, which is why the `a` and `d` rows in `asmConstraints` above are not hypothetical.
★ THE RESULT IS NOT A RESULT — it is a REGISTER PAIR. `result: none` plus implicitRegisters, exactly like `cqo`/`mul_high`: the value arrives in EDX:EAX, which no single result slot can name. `outputs ⊆ clobbered` is the schema-loader invariant (regalloc builds its forbidden set from `clobbered`), so both registers appear in both arrays.
★ THE ROLES ARE REUSED, NOT MINTED. `high`/`low` already exist in `kKnownImplicitRegisterRoles` — added for the 128-bit MUL projection, where they mean exactly what they mean here: the two halves of one wide value split across two registers. A new `tscHigh`/`tscLow` pair would have been a per-instruction verb set for a shape the vocabulary already had. Roles matter because a reorder of the positional arrays can otherwise silently swap which half a consumer captures — and swapping RDTSC's halves multiplies every measured interval by 2^32.
★ `hasSideEffects: true`, and here it guards a REAL miscompile rather than a hypothetical one: RDTSC is not a function of its (empty) operand list — two reads must return two values. A pure declaration invites CSE to fold two reads into one, at which point EVERY elapsed-time measurement in the program is exactly ZERO, and invites LICM to hoist the read out of the loop being timed. ⚠ Same honest scope as `nop`: the live CSE/DCE/LICM read the MIR-tier flag today.

D-CSUBSET-DIVISION-OP-CODEGEN — signed-divide single op (cycle 10r split). IDIV r/m64 divides RDX:RAX by operand 0 (modrm.rm), placing quotient in RAX + remainder in RDX. Encoder auto-computes REX with W=1 + B=(operand 0's high bit), correctly handling R8-R15 operands. Cycle 10r split from the prior compound encoding to fix REX-prefix overlap silent-miscompile (see cqo $comment). implicitRegisters: inputs=[rax,rdx] (IDIV reads RDX:RAX as 128-bit dividend); outputs=[rax,rdx] (quotient + remainder); clobbered=[rax,rdx] (both prior values destroyed — required by the schema-loader `outputs ⊆ clobbered` invariant added in the 10r 7-agent review fold, since regalloc consumes `clobbered` to build its forbidden set). inputRoles/outputRoles (D-CSUBSET-MOD-OP-CODEGEN-OUTPUT-INDEX-CONTRACT, 2026-06-10): the MIR→LIR div/mod lowering pins the dividend + captures the quotient (SDiv) or remainder (SMod) BY ROLE — a reorder of the positional arrays can no longer silently flip the projected register.

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: idiv r/m32 — 0xF7 /7 without REX.W (divides EDX:EAX, quotient EAX / remainder EDX, both zero-extending into the full registers). Pairs with the width-32 cqo sibling (CDQ).

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-DIVISION-OP-CODEGEN — XOR EDX, EDX as the pre-divide zero-extend for unsigned divide (cycle 10r split). 0x31 0xD2 — 32-bit XOR with explicit dest/src both = EDX. 32-bit op zero-extends to RDX, clearing all 64 bits. No REX prefix (32-bit operands). FLAG 1 silent-miscompile guard at byte-level: the unsigned-divide pre-emit uses ZERO-extend (this op); signed-divide uses SIGN-extend (cqo). implicitRegisters: outputs=[rdx]; clobbered=[rdx]. No inputs declared (the op writes a constant zero, doesn't read the prior RDX value).

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: deliberately WIDTH-ABSENT (match-any). XOR EDX,EDX is ALREADY a 32-bit op that zeroes the full RDX — the same bytes are the correct unsigned-divide pre-op at BOTH widths (the 32-bit DIV reads only EDX of it).

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-DIVISION-OP-CODEGEN — unsigned-divide single op (cycle 10r split). DIV r/m64 divides RDX:RAX by operand 0 (modrm.rm), placing quotient in RAX + remainder in RDX. Encoder auto-computes REX with W=1 + B=(operand 0's high bit). implicitRegisters: inputs=[rax,rdx]; outputs=[rax,rdx]; clobbered=[rax,rdx] (mirrors `idiv_op` — required by the `outputs ⊆ clobbered` invariant). inputRoles/outputRoles mirror `idiv_op` (D-CSUBSET-MOD-OP-CODEGEN-OUTPUT-INDEX-CONTRACT): UDiv captures role 'quotient', UMod captures role 'remainder'.

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: div r/m32 — 0xF7 /6 without REX.W (unsigned 32-bit divide of EDX:EAX; quotient EAX zero-extends).

opcodes.$comment: c103 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-UMULH) — unsigned MUL-HIGH single op. MUL r/m64 (0xF7 /4) multiplies RAX by operand 0 (modrm.rm), placing the 128-bit product's low half in RAX and the HIGH half in RDX. The __umulh intrinsic captures the RDX 'high' outputRole (the RAX low half is discarded). NO pre-op — unlike div's cqo, MUL overwrites RDX:RAX unconditionally, so RDX is output-only and NOT an implicit input (contrast div_op inputs=[rax,rdx]). implicitRegisters honour outputs ⊆ clobbered: inputs=[rax]; outputs/clobbered=[rax,rdx]; inputRoles multiplicand=rax; outputRoles high=rdx (+ low=rax for completeness — the MIR->LIR lowering reads only 'high'). Encoder auto-computes REX with W=1 + B=(operand 0's high bit).

variants.$comment: MUL r/m32 — 0xF7 /4 without REX.W (unsigned 32-bit multiply of EAX; high half in EDX). Present for completeness; the u64 __umulh never selects it.

opcodes.$comment: FC17.9(b) (D-CSUBSET-BITCOUNT-INTRINSICS): POPCNT r, r/m — population count (set bits). F3 0F B8 /r; width 64 adds REX.W (bytes F3 48 0F B8 /r), width 32 no REX.W (F3 0F B8 /r). ModR/M.reg = the GPR destination (resultSlot), ModR/M.rm = the source (wire 0) — the `fpcvt` mandatoryPrefix + modrm.reg-dest shape. The mandatoryPrefix F3 emits BEFORE the auto-REX (the fpcvt/lock_cmpxchg legacy-prefix-then-REX order). MIR Popcount's NATIVE realization; a target NOT declaring `popcount` (arm64) takes the SWAR fallback. `popcount` (verb) not `popcnt` — the DSS internal mnemonic is the semantic verb (a future arm64 NEON CNT would share this slot).

FC17.9(b) (D-CSUBSET-BITCOUNT-INTRINSICS): LZCNT r, r/m — count leading zeros, DEFINED at 0 = operand width (32/64) — unlike BSR (UB at 0). F3 0F BD /r; width 64 adds REX.W. Same modrm.reg-dest + F3-mandatoryPrefix shape as popcount. MIR Clz's NATIVE realization; the DSS verb is `clz` (shared with arm64 CLZ — same semantics, defined =width at 0). Assumes an x86-64 baseline with ABM/LZCNT (as the umulh/cmpxchg intrinsics already assume a modern baseline); a target without it would drop the `clz` row and take the SWAR fallback.

FC17.9(b) (D-CSUBSET-BITCOUNT-INTRINSICS): TZCNT r, r/m — count trailing zeros, DEFINED at 0 = operand width (32/64) — unlike BSF (UB at 0). F3 0F BC /r; width 64 adds REX.W. Same shape. MIR Ctz's NATIVE realization (DSS verb `ctz`); arm64 has no scalar TZCNT and composes RBIT-then-CLZ instead. BMI1 baseline assumption (as LZCNT above).

D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP: BSWAP r — reverse the byte order of a register (Intel SDM Vol. 2A BSWAP). 0F C8+rd; width 64 adds REX.W (48 0F C8+rd). ★ A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM ITS THREE NEIGHBOURS ABOVE, in the one way that matters: BSWAP's destination rides the OPCODE BYTE (+rd), not ModR/M — the instruction has no ModR/M byte at all — and it is destructive (dest == source). So it is declared `requires2Address: true` with the operand-0 wire in `opcode.reg` and NO `resultSlot`, exactly like `add`/`not` declare theirs in `modrm.rm`: after `lir_2addr_legalize` inserts `mov result, operands[0]` and rewrites operand 0 to the result register, operand 0 IS the destination, so wiring it places the destination. (target_schema's rule-G `isDestSlot` lists `opcode.reg` for precisely this shape; the `mov r64,imm64` variant uses the same slot but as a `resultSlot`, a different code path.) ★★ NO WIDTH-16 VARIANT, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: `bswap r16` is architecturally undefined (SDM: 'BSWAP with a 16-bit register is undefined'), MEASURED — GAS REFUSES `bswap %ax` outright with 'operand size mismatch', and gcc emits no 16-bit bswap across 20 flag combinations. `_byteswap_ushort` therefore takes mir_to_lir's generic universal-ALU byte-reversal expansion on x86 BY DESIGN; the lowering's capability probe is PER-WIDTH (`opcodeWithWidth`) rather than mnemonic-presence for exactly this reason — a presence-only probe would emit a width-16 bswap that matches no variant here. arm64 needs no such fallback (it declares all three widths: REV16/REV/REV(X)). Both variants below are width-keyed because the schema rejects mixing a width-keyed variant with a width-absent sibling of the same operand shape.

variants.$comment: bswap r32 — 0F C8+rd without REX.W. A 32-bit register write auto-zero-extends to the full 64-bit register, so the u32 result is clean.

opcodes.$comment: c104 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-ATOMIC-CAS) — atomic compare-and-swap, mem-dest: LOCK CMPXCHG [base+disp32], reg (LOCK 0xF0 mandatoryPrefix + 0x0F 0xB1 /r). Semantics: compares RAX/EAX (the implicit 'comparand' input-role) with [mem]; equal -> stores the wired reg (the NEW value, modrm.reg); unequal -> loads [mem] into RAX/EAX. EITHER way RAX ends holding the ORIGINAL observed value (the 'old' output-role the MIR AtomicCas lowering captures). LOCK makes it a full barrier — the correct strength for Win32 InterlockedCompareExchange. Operand shape mirrors `store`'s 4-op mem-dest form: [newval_reg, base_reg, MemBase(scale), MemOffset(disp)]. mandatoryPrefix [240] emits BEFORE the auto-REX (the 0x66 width-16-store precedent — legacy prefixes precede REX, REX immediately precedes the opcode), so a high-numbered base/newval register REX.B/R composes correctly: F0 [REX] 0F B1 /r. Width 32 = the Win32 LONG (LLP64) CAS — NO rexW; width 64 for completeness (a future 64-bit CAS consumer). implicitRegisters: inputs=[rax] (the comparand), outputs/clobbered=[rax] (the observed-original; outputs ⊆ clobbered).

Declared as a distinct slot with the SAME encoding as the scalar `load` (0x8B /r) so the pure-slot-presence probe finds an acquire-load realization on x86 (a target omitting it would fail loud, never silently under-fence). Operand shape [ptr, MemBase(1), MemOffset(0)] (unified with arm64 LDAR): ptr->modrm.rm.mem, result->modrm.reg, disp32=0. VERIFIED by objdump: `mov ecx,[rax]` = 8b 08. Widths 64 (REX.W — i64/pointer) + 32 (int / _Atomic int).

FC17.9(d) atomic Phase C (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): the release/acq_rel realization of MIR AtomicStore on x86-64 — a PLAIN `mov [base+disp32], reg` (x86 stores are ALREADY release). Same encoding as the scalar `store` (0x89 /r). Operand shape [value, ptr, MemBase(1), MemOffset(0)]: value->modrm.reg, ptr->modrm.rm.mem, disp32=0. A `mov` does NOT write its value reg (no clobber hazard, unlike the seq_cst XCHG). VERIFIED by objdump: `mov [rax],ecx` = 89 08. Widths 64 (REX.W) + 32.

FC17.9(d) atomic Phase C (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): the SEQ_CST realization of MIR AtomicStore on x86-64 — `xchg [base+disp32], reg` (0x87 /r). A MEMORY-operand XCHG is IMPLICITLY LOCK'd (Intel SDM Vol.2B XCHG: the LOCK protocol is automatic whenever a memory operand is referenced, no LOCK prefix needed) = a FULL fence, the correct strength for a seq_cst store. ★ XCHG WRITES the OLD memory value back into its reg operand, so `lowerAtomicStore` COPIES the stored value into a fresh scratch first — else a live-after value vreg is corrupted. Operand shape [value(scratch), ptr, MemBase(1), MemOffset(0)] (same as `store`): value->modrm.reg, ptr->modrm.rm.mem. VERIFIED by objdump: `xchg dword [rax],ecx` = 87 08, `xchg qword [rax],rcx` = 48 87 08. Widths 64 (REX.W) + 32.

D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-FENCE (+ D-CSUBSET-SYNC-BUILTIN-BARRIER): MFENCE — the STANDALONE seq_cst CPU fence MIR AtomicFence (__sync_synchronize) lowers to. 0F AE F0, MEASURED via clang -c -arch x86_64 + otool -t on `__sync_synchronize()` (this machine, 2026-07-30). Zero operands, no result, no ModR/M — a fixed 3-byte instruction (the xor_rdx_zero match-any shape; deliberately WIDTH-ABSENT, a fence has no operand width). hasSideEffects=true so no LIR pass drops or reorders it. Distinct from store_seqcst above (xchg — a fence FUSED to a store): this is the fence ALONE, for the store-less __sync_synchronize call sites (sqlite3MemoryBarrier).

BOTH HALVES WERE TRUE WHEN THEY WERE TYPED AND FALSE WHEN THE COMMIT LANDED, so they are CORRECTED in place rather than deleted — the reasoning beneath them is exactly why the fix had to exist (D-COMMENT-A-CLAIM-TRUE-WHEN-TYPED-AND-FALSE-WHEN-THE-COMMIT-LANDED). ✔RE-MEASURED at the CLI 2026-08-24, x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec AND x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec, debug AND release: ONE program spelling BOTH directions — an `__asm__ goto` comparing an `"m"` operand against an `"r"` one as `cmpq %reg, mem` and then as `cmpq mem, %reg` — compiles rc=0 and RUNS returning 42, so each direction branches on the flags of the comparison it actually writes and neither encodes the other. ★★★ WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION IS THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THAT AXIS HAD TO BE INVENTED. `AsmInstructionLowering::buildLirInst` builds the memory-DESTINATION list for `cmpq %r14, mem` and the memory-SOURCE list for `cmpq mem, %r14` as the SAME four kinds `[reg, reg, membase, memoffset]`, and the two mean `mem - r14` (0x39 /r) and `r14 - mem` (0x3B /r) — opposite operand orders, different flags for every signed comparison. Every other arithmetic mnemonic escapes that collision because it PRODUCES a value: its memory-destination direction lives on a `result: none` sibling (`add_mem`, `sub_mem`, …) elected from the consumer set while its memory-source direction is a variant on the producer, and the engine withholds the register-destination shape entirely while a memory operand is present AND the row lists a producer. `cmp` is ALREADY `result: none`, so it has no producer to trigger that withholding and no second candidate set to separate the directions — which is precisely why the direction could not be carried by the CANDIDATE SET here and had to be carried on the INSTRUCTION instead. ⚠ THE OPERATIONAL RULE THE CORRECTED SENTENCE WAS PROTECTING IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDING, which is why it is restated rather than dropped: a `["reg", "reg", "membase", "memoffset"]` sibling added to this opcode WITHOUT `memoryDestination` on BOTH members of the pair is a silent miscompile, not a feature.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-WHILE-LOOP-SUBSTRATE (step 13.5 cycle 1, 2026-06-03): materialize 0/1 byte from FLAGS by cond-code. Encoding `0F 90+cc /0 r8` — the LOW 4 BITS of the SECOND opcode byte carry the condition (resolved via the target's `condCodeEncoding` table from the inst's payload). Result is r8 (low byte of a GPR); upper bits left undefined per Intel SDM. The LIR substrate treats setcc's result as a GPR vreg — callers either compare against 0 immediately (cmp r64, imm32 with sign-extend; safe for boolean compare since AL=0/1) or zero-extend via a follow-up movzx. Cycle scope keeps the substrate minimal; D-LIR-SETCC-MOVZX-COMPOUND anchors the zero-extend pairing when a boolean must escape into a fully-extended 64-bit slot.

★★★ THE 8-BIT-KEYED TWIN, AND IT IS DECLARED FIRST ON PURPOSE (D-ASM-X86-NO-8BIT-REGISTER-FILE, 2026-08-13). `0F 90+cc /0 r8` writes a BYTE register and always did; what was missing was any variant SAYING so, and the consequence was that gas's `sete %al` — the only spelling gas accepts — could not be shipped. The text-lowering derives width 8 from `%al`, and `variantHonorsDeclaredWidth` refuses a width-absent variant at any width other than the target's natural 64, so without this row `sete %al` failed loud and `sete %rax` (which gas REJECTS) was the only form DSS could take: bidirectional non-conformance.
★ VARIANT ORDER IS THE MECHANISM: `selectEncodingVariant` is FIRST-MATCH, so an 8-bit instruction takes this row and a 64-bit one falls through to the width-absent row below. ✔MEASURED that the fall-through is required: the C path (`lowerICmp` in mir_to_lir.cpp) emits `setcc` with DEFAULT flags, i.e. width 64, and making the existing row width-8 instead of adding this one would have broken every C compare.
⚠ THE TEMPLATE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL to the row below, including `forceRexPrefix` — the encoder reads width ONLY to select a variant, never to choose a prefix, so the two rows differ in what they MATCH and not in what they EMIT.

The 64-bit sibling. ⚠ IT IS WIDTH-KEYED RATHER THAN MATCH-ANY, AND THE LOADER IS WHAT INSISTED: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13, leaving it width-absent alongside the 8-bit row above fails load with `C_MalformedJson … variants 0 and 1 share operandKinds but mix a width-keyed guard with a width-absent (match-any) one` (convergence-fix D / D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS). That rule exists precisely so a match-any sibling cannot shadow a width-discriminated one, which is the shape this pair would otherwise have had. 64 is the width the C path's `setcc` already carries (default flags), so keying it changes nothing there.
variants.$templateComment: D-LIR-SETCC-WIDTH-CONTRACT (step 13.5 cycle 1 post-fold, code-reviewer C2): `forceRexPrefix: true` forces a REX prefix even when no W/R/X/B bit is set. Required so the byte-register-bearing setcc accesses spl/bpl/sil/dil (low byte of r4..r7) instead of the legacy ah/ch/dh/bh high-byte aliases. Without this, regalloc picking rsp/rbp/rsi/rdi would silently write the setcc result into the HIGH byte of a DIFFERENT physical register.

opcodes.$comment: Hard-trap / 'this code path is unreachable'. AS1 maps to x86_64 ud2 (encoding `0F 0B`). Encoding added at D-LK10-ENTRY Slice A (2026-06-02) so the trampoline emitter can append `unreachable` after noreturn syscall / call_indirect_via_extern call sites — reaches `assemble()` and must emit bytes (the `TargetEncodingShape::None` arm in `asm.cpp` fails loud `A_NoEncodingDeclared`). Shape mirrors the `ret` opcode (zero-operand variant, no ModR/M, opcode bytes literal).

D-LK10-ENTRY Slice A: raw kernel transition (Linux exit_group / Mach-O BSD exit). Zero-operand, no result, no successors, NOT a terminator (general-case opcode: FF6 hello-world's `write` syscall returns to the next instruction; only the trampoline's `exit` syscall is noreturn, and that's signaled by the trampoline emitter appending a separate `unreachable` after). Encoding: x86_64 SYSCALL `0F 05` — fixed 2-byte opcode, same shape vocabulary as `ret` and the new `unreachable`. The syscall-number register is loaded into `rax` (or per the target's `syscallNumGpr` field on format schema's `processExit` — Slice B) by a preceding LIR `mov` op, NOT a payload on `syscall` itself.

D-LK10-ENTRY Slice A: indirect call through an extern-import IAT slot (Windows kernel32!ExitProcess, future macOS libSystem imports). x86_64 encoding `FF 15 disp32` (call qword ptr [RIP + disp32]) — the same 4-byte disp32 + REL32 reloc shape as the existing direct `call` opcode (E8 disp32), just with a 2-byte opcode literal `[255, 21]` (FF + ModR/M byte 15h = mod=00 reg=/2 rm=101 → [RIP+disp32]). NOT a terminator (general-case indirect call; the trampoline emitter appends `unreachable` after when the callee is noreturn like ExitProcess). 1 operand = ExternImport SymbolRef. The `rel32` reloc-kind row (in this file's `relocations[]` array) computes `S - P - 4` which is exactly what `[RIP+disp32]` resolution needs at load time (S = IAT slot VA, P = the disp32 patch site, RIP at execution = patch + 4). D-LK10-ENTRY-ML7-FRAME-BIAS-UNIFY post-fold (2026-06-02): result widened from `none` to `optional` — same shape as `call` — so MIR→LIR's `lowerCall` can emit `call_indirect_via_extern` for an extern returning a non-void value (puts returns int). The materialize pass moves the return register into the result vreg uniformly for both `call` and `call_indirect_via_extern`; the schema's result-rule must permit both void and non-void targets.

D-CSUBSET-WHILE-LOOP-SUBSTRATE (step 13.5 cycle 1, 2026-06-03): unconditional intra-function jump. Encoding `E9 rel32` (5 bytes). The 4-byte trailing rel32 is resolved at assemble-time via the BlockRel32 slot + per-function patch list (NOT a linker relocation — intra-function only). Operand[0] is a BlockRef naming the target basic block.

D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: indirect branch `jmp r/m64` — 0xFF /4 (jmp rax = FF E0). Mirrors `call`'s 0xFF /2 indirect form: NO REX.W (FF /4 defaults to 64-bit in long mode); REX.B derives from the register's high ordinal bit. Operand[0] is the target-address register; successors = all address-taken blocks (terminatorKind indirect-br, variadic successors). The MIR IndirectBr lowers to this; the address register is materialized from a preceding `lea` of the target block's synthetic symbol (BlockAddress).

D-CSUBSET-WHILE-LOOP-SUBSTRATE (step 13.5 cycle 1, 2026-06-03): conditional intra-function jump with mandatory fallthrough. Compound encoding `0F 8x rel32; E9 rel32` (11 bytes total). The cond nibble in 0x80's low 4 bits comes from the inst's payload (TargetCondCode) via the schema's condCodeEncoding table. Both target blocks pass as BlockRef operands: operand[0] = ifTrue (taken when cond holds — encoded as the first rel32); operand[1] = ifFalse (the fallthrough — encoded as the trailing `E9 rel32`). The wire-1's `prefixOpcodeBytes: [0xE9]` bridges the two displacements. A future optimizer pass elides the trailing jmp when ifFalse is the next-laid-out block (anchored D-OPT-JCC-FALLTHROUGH).

call — direct AND indirect near call, one mnemonic with per-callee-kind variants (FC4 c2). Direct `call sym`: 0xE8 + 4-byte signed PC-relative displacement (filled with 0 by the assembler; the linker patches via the rel32 relocation). Indirect `call reg` (function-pointer callee): 0xFF /2 with the callee register in ModR/M.rm — NO REX.W (FF /2 defaults to 64-bit operand size in long mode); REX.B derives automatically from the register's high ordinal bit (call r10 = 41 FF D2). Keeping both under ONE mnemonic (a variant, not a second opcode) keeps isCall / functionHasCalls / caller-saved-clobber semantics shared by construction. The schema's maxOperands=255 admits a call ABI where extra operands carry arg-register hints; the callconv materializer emits the single-operand forms.

variants.$comment: FC4 c2: call r/m64 — 0xFF /2 (indirect call through a register; call rax = FF D0). No width key: FF /2 is 64-bit by default in long mode, so the variant matches any declared operation width. /digit precedent: idiv /7, div /6, shl /4.

opcodes.$comment: ret — 0xC3 near-return. The schema's maxOperands=1 admits an optional return value carrier; AS2 cycle 2 wires the zero-operand variant only. The actual return value is materialized into the calling-convention's return register by ML7 callconv-lowering BEFORE the ret instruction is emitted (via a `mov` to rax/xmm0); the ret instruction itself never carries an operand at the byte level.

Cycle 3c is the pass-through layer: payload is threaded verbatim from MIR Alloca (currently 0 — MIR does not yet encode size/align; that lands when ML6's frame-layout phase pulls on it). Result is a pointer-class virtreg holding the slot's effective address. AS1 turns this into a frame-relative `lea` once the frame layout is known.

Load from memory. Operands: [base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)]. Optional index-reg arm added in cycle 3d. Emits `mov reg, [base + disp]`: REX.W 0x8B /r ModR/M(mod=10, reg=result, rm=base) [SIB 0x24 when base.lo3==4] disp32. Plan 13 §3.1 D-AS4-1 — landed alongside ML7 cycle 2 to close D-LK10-2 byte-on-disk path.

variants.$comment: 3-op no-index form, width 64: `mov reg, [base + disp32]` (REX.W 0x8B). Width-keyed (was width-absent) now that the byte form below is declared — convergence-fix D forbids mixing a match-any sibling with a width-keyed one of the SAME operandKinds. Every GPR integer/pointer load carries width 64 (memAccessWidthFlags returns 0 ⇒ width 64 for non-Char GPR types — full-slot read, value-correct since loaded ints are consumed low-bits-only).

3-op no-index form, width 8 (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN): `movzx reg, byte [base + disp32]` (REX.W 0F B6 /r). A char/byte memory access MUST be byte-EXACT — a 64-bit read of a 1-byte string/array element reads 7 bytes past it (a fault at a section/page edge). ZERO-extend (movzx) is deliberate: the load is a SIGNEDNESS-AGNOSTIC byte fetch — sign semantics live in the explicit cast that follows (SExt for signed `char`, ZExt for unsigned `byte`), each of which re-reads the low byte, so the load's upper bits never reach a consumer un-recast (C integer-promotion always widens a char operand before arithmetic). REX.W sets the r64 dest (its low 8 hold the byte); the memory source has no high-byte-alias hazard (that is a register-source-only concern). Selected when the Load's result type is Char (width 8 on the LIR inst, via memAccessWidthFlags).

3-op no-index form, width 32 (D-LIR-INT-MEMORY-WIDTH-EXACT): `mov r32, [base + disp32]` (0x8B WITHOUT REX.W). A 4-byte int load MUST be width-exact — a 64-bit read of a PACKED int (an array element / struct field, NOT a stand-alone scalar local) reads 4 bytes past it (the store peer clobbers the neighbour / overruns the frame slot — the bug the array-storage cycle exposed). A 32-bit register write auto-zero-extends bits 63:32 (Intel SDM MOV), so the int lands clean in the full register. Selected when the Load's result type is a 4-byte integer (I32/U32, or `long` under LLP64) — width 32 via memAccessWidthFlags.

3-op no-index form, width 16 (D-LIR-INT-MEMORY-WIDTH-EXACT): `movzx r32, word [base + disp32]` (0F B7 /r, no REX.W). A 2-byte short load must be half-word-exact — a wider read of a packed short reads past it. ZERO-extend (movzx) is the signedness-agnostic half-word fetch (the width-8 char movzx peer at 0F B6); the short→int promote cast that follows re-reads the low 16 bits (SExt/ZExt-16 = D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS, not yet encoded ⇒ short VALUE use fails loud, never silently miscompiles). Selected when the Load's result type is I16/U16 — width 16 via memAccessWidthFlags.
4-op indexed form (D-AS4-5), width 64: `mov reg, [base + index*scale + disp32]` (REX.W 0x8B). The walker emits SIB unconditionally when SibIndex wires.

4-op indexed form, width 8 (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN): `movzx reg, byte [base + index*scale + disp32]` (REX.W 0F B6 /r + SIB). The byte-exact + signedness-agnostic rationale is the 3-op width-8 form's; this arm serves a runtime-index char-array access (`arr[i]`, scale 1 since sizeof(char)==1).

This ONE row therefore serves ELF and PE with config-only differences — the target JSON stays format-blind. Opcode 0x8B = MOV r64, r/m64 (register form of the load); result rides ModR/M.reg. opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c1 (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS shifts residue): logical left shift — FIRST real encodings. Intel SDM SHL: the VARIABLE-count form `SHL r/m64, CL` = REX.W D3 /4 (the count is the IMPLICIT CL register — x86 has no 3-address reg-count shift); the CONSTANT-count form `SHL r/m64, imm8` = REX.W C1 /4 ib; 32-bit siblings = the same opcodes WITHOUT REX.W per the FC3-c2 width axis (a 32-bit shift auto-zero-extends its destination). Hardware masks the count to the operand width (& 63 / & 31, SDM Vol. 2B SAL/SAR/SHL/SHR) — C declares counts >= width UB (C23 6.5.7p3), so no extra masking is emitted; whatever the hardware does to a UB count is conforming. 2-address: the r/m operand IS the destination (requires2Address legalize inserts the copy). implicitRegisters (the FC1 idiv role-contract pattern): inputs=[rcx] (the core reads CL), inputRoles={count: rcx} — the MIR->LIR shift lowering pins the count vreg BY ROLE, never by name; clobbered=[rcx] expresses that the REALIZATION's count-pin mov destroys RCX's prior value across the sequence (regalloc's covered-position exclusion keeps live ranges out of RCX across the shift — the same mechanism that keeps div operands out of RAX/RDX). The exclusion is conservatively also active at imm-form positions (the constraint is per-OPCODE; costs one register of pressure there, never correctness). The lowering selects the imm8 variant when the count is a MIR Const in [0,255] AND a [reg,imm] variant is declared; otherwise the CL pair.

opcodes.$comment: Float arithmetic (cycle 3d FPR wave). FC2 Part B: ADDSD xmm1, xmm2 — F2 0F 58 /r (scalar double add). Mandatory prefix F2 selects the scalar-double form and is emitted BEFORE the auto-REX (xmm8-15 operands set REX.R/REX.B with rexW=false). 2-address like `mul`: dest goes to ModR/M.reg (op[0] IS the destination after lir_2addr_legalize), source-2 to ModR/M.rm. FC3.5 sweep-c2 (D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN): the F32 sibling ADDSS xmm1, xmm2 = F3 0F 58 /r (Intel SDM ADDSS — same opcode bytes, the F3 scalar-single mandatory prefix) rides the width axis: the F64 variant is now width-KEYED 64, the F32 one 32 (an F32-typed MIR FAdd carries kLirInstFlagWidth32 via widthFlagsForType).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: ADDSS xmm1, xmm2 — F3 0F 58 /r (scalar single).

opcodes.$comment: Float subtract — SUBSD xmm1, xmm2 = F2 0F 5C /r (scalar double) / SUBSS = F3 0F 5C /r (scalar single), Intel SDM SUBSD/SUBSS. Cluster-F F3 (float_mul_sub): encoding added, mirroring fadd/fdiv (opcode 0F 5C vs fadd 0F 58). NON-COMMUTATIVE: dest=op[0] (the minuend) -> ModR/M.reg, op[1] (the subtrahend) -> ModR/M.rm, so `a - b` = reg(a) - rm(b) (same dest=ModR/M.reg convention as fdiv). 2-address (requires2Address): op[0] IS the destination after lir_2addr_legalize.

variants.$comment: SUBSS xmm1, xmm2 — F3 0F 5C /r (scalar single).
