variants.$comment: MULSS xmm1, xmm2 — F3 0F 59 /r (scalar single).

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2: float divide — DIVSD xmm1, xmm2 = F2 0F 5E /r (scalar double) / DIVSS = F3 0F 5E /r (scalar single), Intel SDM DIVSD/DIVSS. Same 2-address dest=ModR/M.reg shape as fadd (division is non-commutative: op[0] IS the dividend/destination after lir_2addr_legalize, op[1] the divisor in ModR/M.rm). First consumer: NaN construction (0.0/0.0) for the D-COND-FLOAT-NAN-TRUTHINESS-FCMP corpus witnesses — this also closes the fdiv encoding stub.

variants.$comment: FC3.5: DIVSS xmm1, xmm2 — F3 0F 5E /r (scalar single).

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (FCmp LIR lowering): float compare writing FLAGS, no register result — the float sibling of `cmp`. UCOMISD xmm1, xmm2 = 66 0F 2E /r (scalar double) / UCOMISS xmm1, xmm2 = NP 0F 2E /r (scalar single — NO prefix; an F3 here would be an invalid encoding), Intel SDM UCOMISD/UCOMISS. Quiet (non-signaling on QNaN) compare: sets ZF/PF/CF — unordered → ZF=PF=CF=1, greater → all 0, less → CF=1, equal → ZF=1 (the truth table the float condCodeEncoding arms below realize; full derivation at mir_to_lir floatCmpPlan). ModRM roles: ModR/M.reg = operand[0] (the LEFT side of the predicate), ModR/M.rm = operand[1] — NOTE this is the RM-form direction, the MIRROR of the integer cmp's 0x39 MR-form wiring; the LIR-level convention (op[0] = left) is identical. Annex-F note: C's relational operators are SIGNALING comparisons (COMISD raises Invalid on quiet NaN); DSS does not model the FP environment (no fenv access), so the quiet UCOMI forms serve all predicates — the comparison RESULTS are identical, only the unmodeled FE_INVALID flag differs.

variants.$comment: FC3.5: UCOMISS xmm1, xmm2 — NP 0F 2E /r (no mandatory prefix).

opcodes.$comment: Float unary negate (the ABSTRACT MIR FNeg's LIR mnemonic). x86 has NO native fp-negate instruction, so this opcode carries NO encoding: `lowerFNeg` in mir_to_lir probes this opcode's declared-encoding presence (empty here) and takes the CAPABILITY fallback — mint a 16-byte rodata sign-mask + emit `fneg_mask` (xorpd/xorps reg, [rip+mask]) below. On arm64 the same-named `fneg` opcode DOES declare a native FNEG encoding, so the probe there emits it directly. Keeping this abstract-but-declared (rather than deleting it) preserves the MnemonicSlot::FNeg probe target that distinguishes the two realizations by capability (c78, D-CSUBSET-FLOAT-NEG-ENCODING).

c78 (D-CSUBSET-FLOAT-NEG-ENCODING): the x86 realization of float negate — XOR the value against a 16-byte rodata SIGN-MASK (bit 63 set for F64 / bit 31 for F32, high bytes zero). This is gcc's `xorpd xmm0, XMMWORD PTR .LC0[rip]`, chosen for IEEE exactness: XOR flips ONLY the sign bit, so -(+0.0)=-0.0, -(-0.0)=+0.0, and -NaN preserves the payload — the `0.0 - x` alternative gives +0.0 for x=+0.0 (wrong signed zero) and mishandles NaN. `lowerFNeg` mints an anonymous 16-byte, 16-byte-aligned CONST rodata global (a U128 whose low qword/dword holds the mask, emitted via the existing float-literal-promotion mint mechanism) and materializes its address, then emits this op with operands [value, maskSymbol]. 2-address (requires2Address): the destination xmm = ModR/M.reg (op[0], the value; the legalize inserts `movaps dst, value`), the mask is ModR/M.rm via the RIP-relative disp32 slot (mod=00 rm=101 + a rel32 relocation against the mask symbol — the SAME `riprel.disp32` slot `movsd_load`/`lea` use). SSE m128 requires the memory operand be 16-byte aligned at runtime — the mint's 16-byte alignment + the section-alignment layout guarantee it on ELF (sh_addralign) and PE (4KB sectionAlignment, a multiple of 16). F64 = XORPD 66 0F 57 /r (width 64); F32 = XORPS 0F 57 /r (NP, width 32).

variants.$comment: F64: XORPD xmm, [rip+mask] — 66 0F 57 /r. Mirrors the fadd/fmul 2-address shape (NO explicit resultSlot — the result register IS op[0], guaranteed by the requires2Address legalize's `movaps dst, value` + operands[0]:=result rewrite; wire index:0 writes ModR/M.reg = that register). op[1] (mask symbol) -> the riprel.disp32 slot (mod=00 rm=101 + a rel32 reloc against the mask symbol).
F32: XORPS xmm, [rip+mask] — NP 0F 57 /r (no mandatory prefix — a 66 here would be XORPD). Same operand roles + riprel mask as the F64 form.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): x87 80-bit `long double` FLD — load an m80 extended-real from memory and PUSH it onto st0. Intel SDM: DB /5 FLD m80fp ("Push m80fp onto the FPU register stack"). THE MODEL (zero regalloc changes): the x87 stack (st0-7) is INVISIBLE to the flat linear-scan allocator — an F80 value lives in MEMORY (a fresh body-local `alloca` home / a global / the source address), and every F80 op is a FIXED memory→memory instruction sequence (fld;fld;fXXXp;fstp) that starts+ends with an EMPTY stack, using st0/st1 as transient scratch — exactly the idiv implicit-RAX/RDX precedent. ONE base+disp32 memory variant mirroring movsd_load's [base,membase,memoffset] form: operand[0] = the ADDRESS register (modrm.rm.mem → mod=10 + disp32), [1]=MemBase(scale), [2]=MemOffset(disp). modrmRegExt=5 fills ModR/M.reg with the /5 opcode-extension digit; there is NO register RESULT (the push target st0 is implicit), so the encoder emits `DB /5 [modrm 0b10_101_rrr] disp32`. result:none + hasSideEffects — the x87-stack mutation must never be reordered or DCE'd (fld feeds the following fXXXp/fstp only through the implicit stack, which no vreg dep expresses). NO rip-relative variant: an F80 address is ALWAYS materialized into a GPR base first (globalAddrRiprelFoldsIntoLoad walls the fold for F80), so the base+disp form serves every site.

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): x87 80-bit FSTP — POP st0 and store it as an m80 extended-real to memory. Intel SDM: DB /7 FSTP m80fp ("Copy ST(0) to m80fp and pop the register stack"). The closing move of every F80 op's memory→memory sequence (fld;fld;fXXXp;fstp [dst]) and the second half of an F80 value copy (fld [src];fstp [dst]). Same base+disp memory operand shape as fld_m80 — operand[0]=address reg (modrm.rm.mem), [1]=MemBase(scale), [2]=MemOffset(disp); the STORED value is the implicit st0 (NO value operand, unlike movsd_store's 4-op [value,base,membase,memoffset]). modrmRegExt=7 = the /7 digit → `DB /7 [modrm 0b10_111_rrr] disp32`. result:none + hasSideEffects (writes memory + pops the stack).

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): FADDP ST(1),ST(0) = DE C1 (Intel SDM: "Add ST(0) to ST(1), store result in ST(1), and pop the register stack" — the DE C0+i family, i=1). A BARE 2-byte fixed opcode, ZERO operands, no ModR/M (st1/st0 are implicit). Emitted between the two fld_m80 pushes and the fstp_m80: after `fld a; fld b` the stack is st1=a, st0=b, so FADDP leaves st0 = a+b (commutative — direction irrelevant). result:none + hasSideEffects (mutates + pops the implicit x87 stack; must stay ordered relative to the surrounding fld/fstp).

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): FSUBP ST(1),ST(0) = DE E9 (Intel SDM: "Subtract ST(0) from ST(1), store result in ST(1), and pop the register stack" — the DE E8+i family, i=1 → ST(1) ← ST(1) − ST(0)). DIRECTION CRUX: the lowering pushes a THEN b (`fld a; fld b` → st1=a, st0=b), so FSUBP computes st1−st0 = a−b — exactly C's `a - b`. NOT the reversed FSUBRP (DE E1 = ST(0)−ST(1) = b−a). NB the encoder emits the raw BYTES DE E9, so the historical GAS AT&T fsubp/fsubrp mnemonic swap does not apply here. Bare 2-byte fixed opcode, 0 operands. result:none + hasSideEffects.

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): FMULP ST(1),ST(0) = DE C9 (Intel SDM: "Multiply ST(1) by ST(0), store result in ST(1), and pop the register stack" — the DE C8+i family, i=1). After `fld a; fld b` the stack is st1=a, st0=b → st0 = a*b (commutative). Bare 2-byte fixed opcode, 0 operands. result:none + hasSideEffects.

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): FDIVP ST(1),ST(0) = DE F9 (Intel SDM: "Divide ST(1) by ST(0), store result in ST(1), and pop the register stack" — the DE F8+i family, i=1 → ST(1) ← ST(1) / ST(0)). DIRECTION CRUX: after `fld a; fld b` (st1=a, st0=b), FDIVP computes st1/st0 = a/b — exactly C's `a / b`. NOT the reversed FDIVRP (DE F1 = ST(0)/ST(1) = b/a). Raw-byte encoding (DE F9), so the GAS mnemonic swap is irrelevant. Bare 2-byte fixed opcode, 0 operands. result:none + hasSideEffects.

D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH (LD-1): FISTTP m32int = DB /1 (Intel SDM: "Store ST(0) with TRUNCATION to m32int and pop the register stack"). The F80→int conversion tail (FPToSI from long double): `fld_m80 [src]; fisttp_m32 [slot]; mov r32,[slot]`. FISTTP is SSE3 (universally present on every x86_64 CPU and under qemu) and truncates toward zero WITHOUT touching the x87 control word — the C cast's round-toward-zero semantics for free (the strict-baseline fldcw/fistp/fldcw alternative needs a control-word rodata const + 2 extra ops). Same base+disp memory operand shape as fld_m80/fstp_m80; modrmRegExt=1 = the /1 digit. result:none + hasSideEffects (writes m32 + pops st0). m64int (DD /1, for `(long long)ld`) is a later slice — this row serves the (int) cast.

Float-to-float precision change (FPTrunc f64→f32, FPExt f32→f64). FC3.5 sweep-c2: encoded — CVTSD2SS xmm1, xmm2 = F2 0F 5A /r (double→single) and CVTSS2SD xmm1, xmm2 = F3 0F 5A /r (single→double), Intel SDM CVTSD2SS/CVTSS2SD: SAME opcode bytes, the mandatory prefix names the SOURCE width. The width axis therefore keys on the SOURCE: the MIR→LIR FPTrunc/FPExt arm threads a widthOverride from the source operand's type (the result-width default would select exactly the WRONG sibling — FPTrunc's F32 result would pick the F3 widen). ModR/M.reg = the xmm destination (resultSlot), ModR/M.rm = the xmm source.

variants.$comment: F64 source → CVTSD2SS (narrow to single).
F32 source → CVTSS2SD (widen to double).

opcodes.$comment: Float-to-signed-integer conversion (FPToSI). FC2 Part B: CVTTSD2SI r64, xmm — F2 REX.W 0F 2C /r (truncating scalar-double → signed 64-bit). Operand roles per Intel SDM: ModR/M.reg = the GPR DESTINATION (resultSlot), ModR/M.rm = the xmm SOURCE. REX.W widens the destination to r64 (the sign-extended result also serves i32 results — the backend's i32-in-r64 convention). FC3.5 sweep-c2: the F32-source sibling CVTTSS2SI r64, xmm = F3 REX.W 0F 2C /r (Intel SDM CVTTSS2SI — REX.W stays: the destination is still the 64-bit GPR). The width axis keys on the SOURCE float width (the MIR→LIR FPToSI arm threads a widthOverride from the source operand's type; the result-width default — an I32 result → 32 — would mis-key the source axis).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: CVTTSS2SI r64, xmm — F3 REX.W 0F 2C /r (truncating scalar-single → signed 64-bit).

opcodes.$comment: Float-to-unsigned-integer conversion (FPToUI). c78 (D-CSUBSET-FP-TO-UI-CODEGEN): for the c-subset's in-range needs (a double/float whose value fits the U32 result — sqlite's usage), the truncating signed CVTTSD2SI/CVTTSS2SI r64 form serves: any value in [0, 2^32) fits the signed-64 result exactly, and the U32 result reads the low 32 bits (gcc emits the identical `cvttsd2si rax, xmm0` for `(unsigned)d`). SAME encoding + operand roles + SOURCE-width axis as fp_to_si: ModR/M.reg = the GPR destination (resultSlot), ModR/M.rm = the xmm source; REX.W keeps the 64-bit destination. Full correct unsigned-i64 (a double ≥ 2^63 → the conditional-subtract sequence) is deferred as D-CSUBSET-UI-FROM-FP-UNSIGNED-I64; sqlite does not hit it.

variants.$comment: F64 source → CVTTSD2SI r64, xmm — F2 REX.W 0F 2C /r (truncating scalar-double → signed 64-bit; the low 32 bits are the in-range U32 result).
F32 source → CVTTSS2SI r64, xmm — F3 REX.W 0F 2C /r.

opcodes.$comment: Signed-integer-to-float (SIToFP) — the REVERSE of fp_to_si above. CVTSI2SD xmm, r/m = F2 [REX.W] 0F 2A /r (Intel SDM: scalar signed-int -> double). Operand roles MIRROR cvttsd2si SWAPPED: ModR/M.reg = the xmm DESTINATION (resultSlot — the result is FPR-class via the F64 MIR result type, regClassFor), ModR/M.rm = the GPR SOURCE (wire 0). The width axis here keys on the SOURCE INTEGER width (the MIR->LIR SIToFP arm threads a widthOverride from the source operand's int type): a 32-bit source -> the no-REX.W form CVTSI2SD xmm, r32 (width=32), a 64-bit source -> REX.W CVTSI2SD xmm, r64 (width=64). REX.W selects the 64-bit source-integer interpretation (NOT the dest float width — the dest is fixed F64/sd here). DESIGN NOTE (audit + qemu-arm64 scrutiny): the variant guard offers ONE width axis, but cvtsi2sd/ss needs TWO independent selectors — REX.W (source-int width) AND F2-vs-F3 prefix (dest-float width). The source-int axis MUST vary (i32 vs i64 both occur; REX.W wrong = reads the wrong register width), so it OWNS the width axis; the dest-float prefix is fixed at F2/sd (F64 destination), the dominant + sqlite-blocking case (i64 -> volatile double). int -> F32 (`float f = anInt`, ss/F3) has NO encoding this cycle and FAILS LOUD at the mir_to_lir SIToFP arm (a deferred narrow gap, D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN); sqlite uses `double` only.

variants.$comment: CVTSI2SD xmm, r64 — F2 REX.W 0F 2A /r (64-bit signed source). The sqlite i64 -> double blocker.
CVTSI2SD xmm, r32 — F2 0F 2A /r (32-bit signed source, no REX.W).

opcodes.$comment: Unsigned-integer-to-float (UIToFP). x86 SSE2 has NO direct unsigned-int->float opcode; for the c-subset's needs (where the unsigned value fits the SIGNED range of the next-wider int — true for U32 promoted into a 64-bit cvtsi2sd, and the common case) the same CVTSI2SD path serves. The SOURCE-int-width axis matches si_to_fp: width=64 -> REX.W (a U64 whose top bit is set would mis-convert as negative — a documented x86 SSE2 limitation, not exercised by sqlite's u32/size_t-in-range usage), width=32 -> no-REX.W (a U32 source; cvtsi2sd of a 32-bit reg reads it as signed-32, but a U32 always fits the signed-64 result exactly, so the result is value-correct). Dest fixed F64/sd as in si_to_fp; U->F32 deferred (D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). Full correct-unsigned-i64 handling (the zero-extend + conditional-fixup sequence) is deferred as D-CSUBSET-UI-TO-FP-UNSIGNED-I64; sqlite does not hit it.

variants.$comment: CVTSI2SD xmm, r64 — F2 REX.W 0F 2A /r (64-bit source; see the unsigned-i64 caveat above).
CVTSI2SD xmm, r32 — F2 0F 2A /r (32-bit source; a U32 fits the signed-64 result exactly -> value-correct).

opcodes.$comment: Cross-class bit-pattern move (GPR↔FPR). AS1 emits x86_64 `movq` (the QWord variant). Cycle-3d Bitcast lowers via this opcode whenever src and dst register classes differ; same-class Bitcasts continue to use `mov` (handled by cycle 3c).

FC12b (D-FC12B-WIN64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): xmm→r64 bit-copy — MOVQ r/m64, xmm = 66 REX.W 0F 7E /r (Intel SDM MOVQ, the store-to-GPR direction). The CALLER of a Win64 variadic function duplicates each FP vararg into its matching integer (home) register so the callee's va_arg(double) can read it from the home slot. A SEPARATE opcode from `movq_xclass`: the variant guard keys only on (operandKinds, width) and CANNOT disambiguate the two MOVQ directions (both are `reg`/width-64), and `movq_xclass` is consumed bidirectionally by Bitcast — overloading it would force a silent miscompile on the GPR→FPR Bitcast direction. ModR/M.reg = the xmm SOURCE (the wired source operand → modrm.reg), ModR/M.rm = the r64 DESTINATION (the result vreg → modrm.rm). Byte-pin: `movq rdx, xmm1` = 66 48 0F 7E CA (66 prefix; REX.W=0x48; 0F 7E; ModR/M mod=11 reg=xmm1=001 rm=rdx=010 → 0xCA).

Intrinsic call. Payload = intrinsic id (per HirIntrinsicRegistry / MIR convention). Operands = args. Result is optional (some intrinsics produce values, some don't). AS1 maps the intrinsic id to its concrete sequence (e.g. memcpy, debugtrap, sqrt) per target. Cycle 3e lowers MIR IntrinsicCall to this opcode.

Spill reload pseudo-op. Payload = spill-slot index (LirSpillSlot.v). Result = the reloaded value's physical reg. The encoder/ML7 materializes this as `mov result, [stackPointer + slotOffset]`; the exact stackPointer + offset come from per-target callconv lowering. Target-blind at LIR tier.

Spill store pseudo-op. Payload = spill-slot index. Operand[0] = the physical reg whose value is being stored. The encoder/ML7 materializes this as `mov [stackPointer + slotOffset], operand`. Target-blind at LIR tier.

D-AS-REGALLOC-WIDE-CALL-OPERAND-COUNT (option E): outgoing-stack-arg store carrier. Emitted by the PRE-REGALLOC wide-call lowering pass for every outgoing call argument beyond the cc's register-passed capacity (config: argGprs/argFprs counts + slotAligned). Operand[0] = the arg VALUE vreg (still virtual pre-regalloc — regalloc assigns it, ending its live range HERE at the store instead of at the call, which is why a wide call no longer holds N register-operands). Payload = the arg's OVERFLOW SLOT INDEX (0-based, in outgoing-slot units, monotonic across the call's stacked args in source order — the NSAA cursor). lir_callconv materializes it (post-regalloc) into `store operand, [sp + shadowSpaceBytes + payload*outgoingSlotSize]` — BYTE-IDENTICAL geometry to the pre-existing post-regalloc placement-loop stack store, so the caller-store↔callee-load offset contract is unchanged. No encoding (materialized away). hasSideEffects=true so no pass drops/reorders it off its call.

FC2 Part B: FPR-class register-register copy — MOVAPS xmm1, xmm2 = 0F 28 /r (NO mandatory prefix; the F2-prefixed reg-reg MOVSD form merges into the destination's upper lane, creating a false dependency on dst's prior value — MOVAPS copies the full register, the classic codegen choice). ModR/M.reg = destination (resultSlot), ModR/M.rm = source; xmm8-15 set REX.R/REX.B automatically. Bound to the `fpr` class's `move` slot in registerClassOps[] — consumed by the 2-addr legalize implicit copy, MIR→LIR mov-to-fresh/phi-edge copies, and callconv arg/return moves whenever the register class is FPR.

FC2 Part B: FPR-class 8-byte load — MOVSD xmm, m64 = F2 0F 10 /r. Two variants: (a) the 3-op [base + disp32] form mirroring the universal `load` operand shape ([base_reg, MemBase(scale), MemOffset(disp)]) — what MIR Load-of-pointer lowers to (GlobalAddr → `lea reg, [rip+sym]` materializes the address, this loads through it); (b) the 1-op RIP-relative SymbolRef form mirroring `lea`'s riprel.disp32 variant (F2 0F 10 05 rel32 + rel32 relocation) — byte-pinned now, consumed end-to-end when a GlobalAddr+Load fold peephole lands. Bound to the `fpr` class's `load` slot in registerClassOps[]. The STORE form is `movsd_store` (next row — landed with its first consumer, the ms_x64 FPR saved-reg prologue spill). WIDTH-KEYED since FC3.5 sweep-c2 (D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN closure): the F64 variants (F2, width 64) carry their F32 MOVSS siblings (F3 0F 10, width 32) directly below — see the encoding-level $comment. (Audit-residue sweep c2 corrected the prior 'F64-WIDTH ONLY … when an F32 consumer exists' tail, which the variants below had already contradicted.)

encoding.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN): width-keyed pairs — MOVSD xmm, m64 = F2 0F 10 (8-byte read, width 64) vs MOVSS xmm, m32 = F3 0F 10 (4-byte read, width 32; Intel SDM MOVSS). The MIR→LIR lowerLoad threads the loaded type's width for FPR-class results: an 8-byte movsd read of a 4-byte F32 rodata item would read past the item (potential fault at a section edge) — the width axis makes the access width type-exact. Both operandKinds shapes carry the pair (the loader's keyed/absent-mix rule).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: MOVSS xmm, m32 — F3 0F 10 /r (4-byte load).
FC3.5: the RIP-relative MOVSS form (F3 0F 10 05 rel32) — the F32 mirror of the F64 riprel variant (consumed end-to-end when the GlobalAddr+Load fold peephole lands; byte-pinned now).

opcodes.$comment: FC2 (PE float witness, 2026-06-10): FPR-class 8-byte store — MOVSD m64, xmm = F2 0F 11 /r. ModRM DIRECTION is the load's mirror (Intel SDM): 0F 10 loads (xmm ← r/m), 0F 11 stores (r/m ← xmm) — the ModRM ROLES are identical in both (reg = the xmm, rm = the memory operand); only the opcode's direction bit decides which one is read vs written. One variant: the 4-op [value_reg, base_reg, MemBase(scale), MemOffset(disp)] form mirroring the universal `store` operand shape exactly (value → modrm.reg, base → modrm.rm.mem — emitFrameStore's operand order works unchanged). First consumer: the ms_x64 prologue/epilogue saved-reg spill — Win64 declares xmm6-15 CALLEE-SAVED and regalloc prefers callee-saved, so the FIRST FPR vreg under ms_x64 needs this store (SysV has no callee-saved XMMs, never reached it). Bound to the `fpr` class's `store` slot in registerClassOps[]. The full 16-byte XMM is NOT preserved (Win64 requires only the low 64 bits of xmm6-15 to survive — MOVSD's m64 store IS the ABI contract; the regalloc SPILL path stays width-default 64 accordingly). WIDTH-KEYED since FC3.5 sweep-c2 (D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN closure): the F32 MOVSS store sibling (F3 0F 11, width 32) sits directly below for type-exact value stores — see the encoding-level $comment. (Audit-residue sweep c2 corrected the prior 'F64-WIDTH ONLY … when an F32 consumer exists' tail, which the variant below had already contradicted.)

encoding.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2: width-keyed pair — MOVSD m64, xmm (F2, width 64) vs MOVSS m32, xmm (F3 0F 11, width 32; Intel SDM MOVSS). lowerStore threads the stored VALUE's type width for FPR-class stores (type-exact access width); the regalloc spill path stays width-default 64 over 8-byte slots (value-preserving for both float widths — the F32 value is the low 4 bytes either way).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: MOVSS m32, xmm — F3 0F 11 /r (4-byte store).

$registersComment: Physical register file. Ordinal = position in this array (consumed by `LirReg::id` post-regalloc). Only the registers ML6 regalloc + ML7 callconv reference are declared here — sub-byte aliases (al/ah/bl/...) are omitted until a real consumer needs them. Width is in bytes (8/4/2/1). hwEncoding = ModR/M ordinal the assembler/encoder will read.

registers.$comment: ★★ THE 32-BIT VIEWS — `subOf`'s FIRST REAL CONSUMER (2026-08-13). `subOf` has existed on `TargetRegisterInfo` since ML6, is loaded, is resolved-and-cycle-checked at validate() time, and BOTH allocator paths already skip a row that declares it — with ZERO rows using it. These are the rows. They exist so a hand-written `.s` can WRITE `%eax`: the assembly-text lowering resolves a narrow spelling to its PARENT ordinal (LIR names one register and carries the access width on the INSTRUCTION) and then enforces that the spelling's width matches the mnemonic's — gas rejects both `movl %rax,%ecx` and `movl %eax,%rcx`, and so does this. ⚠ THEY ARE NOT ALLOCATABLE AND CANNOT BECOME SO BY ACCIDENT, AND THE MECHANISM CHANGED ON 2026-08-13 — THIS SENTENCE USED TO NAME ONE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. It said `buildFreeLists` (lir_regalloc.cpp) and `pickScratchRegs` (lir_rewrite.cpp) each `continue` on a non-empty `subOf`, and called cc-list absence 'the second, independent reason'. BOTH skips have been DELETED: ✔MEASURED, they were unreachable defence — `allocatable` is built EXCLUSIVELY from the six calling-convention lists (`lir_regalloc.cpp` buildFreeLists / `lir_rewrite.cpp` collectAllocatable), with no independent source, so a row absent from every cc list could never enter a pool for the skip to catch. What replaced them is a LOAD-TIME REJECTION: `TargetSchemaData::validate()`'s `checkRefs` refuses a calling convention that names a `subOf` register, with `C_MalformedJson` and a JSON path pointing at the offending element. ⇒ one config rule and one loud rejection, not two silent skips — and the rows below are safe because none of them appears in any cc list, which is now enforced rather than merely true. ⚠ THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO END *"the 16-bit views (ax/cx/...) are still NOT declared … no shipped opcode form and no dialect spelling writes a 16-bit register yet"*. THAT TRIGGER FIRED ON 2026-08-23: the AT&T dialect now spells `movw`, and `mov`/`load_subreg`/`store` declare 16-bit forms for it, so the word-view block below landed under the SAME first-consumer rule (D-TARGET-SUBREGISTER-ALIASES) the 32-bit and 8-bit blocks did. The rule is unchanged; only its trigger state is.
registers.name: eax

registers.$comment:
★★★ THE 16-BIT (WORD) VIEWS — landed 2026-08-23 with their FIRST CONSUMER, the AT&T `movw` spelling (D-ASM-SUB-NATIVE-OPERAND-UNUSABLE-IN-INLINE-ASM). Until that spelling existed no shipped opcode form and no dialect row could name a 16-bit register, which is why the 32-bit block above recorded them as deliberately absent.
★ SAME MECHANISM AS THE 32-BIT AND 8-BIT BLOCKS, and deliberately no other: `subOf` names the 64-bit PARENT (one hop, not `eax`), the assembly-text lowering resolves a narrow spelling to the parent ordinal and carries the ACCESS WIDTH on the LIR instruction, and the width cross-check then refuses a spelling whose width disagrees with the mnemonic's suffix — gas rejects `movw %eax, %cx` and so does this.
⚠ NOT ALLOCATABLE, by the mechanism the 32-bit block states: `TargetSchemaData::validate()` REFUSES a calling convention that names a `subOf` register, and the cc lists are the only source `allocatable` is built from.
⚠ THE WORD VIEWS OF rsp/rbp/rsi/rdi ARE `sp`/`bp`/`si`/`di` — the SAME spellings AArch64 uses for its stack pointer, which is harmless because register names are resolved against THIS target's own table and never across targets. Unlike the byte views they need NO REX prefix: the high-byte alias hazard (`ah`/`ch`/`dh`/`bh`) is a BYTE-register-only property of the encoding, and 16-bit forms select their size with the 0x66 prefix instead.
⚠ A `%N` OPERAND DOES NOT NEED THESE ROWS AND THE ROW THAT ASKED FOR THEM SAID OTHERWISE — ✔MEASURED by reading `TemplateHost::resolveRegister`: a bound operand's width comes from `AsmOperandBinding::widthBits`, never from a register NAME, so a `short` operand would substitute at width 16 with this block absent. What these rows buy is the HAND-WRITTEN spelling — `__asm__("movw %ax, %cx")`, which gas accepts — and bidirectional conformance is why they land rather than being skipped as unnecessary.
registers.name: ax

registers.$comment:
★★★ THE 8-BIT VIEWS — the row that made `sete %al` SPELLABLE (D-ASM-X86-NO-8BIT-REGISTER-FILE, 2026-08-13). Before them this file declared 49 registers with NO byte file, and the consequence was BIDIRECTIONAL non-conformance in the sense [[feedback_reference_compilers_are_the_spec]] means it: gas WRITES `sete %al` and DSS could not read it, while the only destination DSS could spell — `%rax` — is one gas REJECTS. Shipping a dialect row that accepts input no reference assembler takes is the same defect as refusing input they do accept.
★ SAME MECHANISM AS THE 32-BIT BLOCK ABOVE, and deliberately no other: `subOf` names the 64-bit PARENT (not `eax` — a two-hop chain would load and resolve identically, and one hop is what the table already reads as 'these are views of that machine register'). The assembly-text lowering resolves a narrow spelling to the parent ordinal and carries the ACCESS WIDTH on the LIR instruction, so `al` and `rax` are one register with two spellings, exactly as `eax` and `rax` are.
⚠ NOT ALLOCATABLE, by the mechanism the 32-bit block states: a calling convention naming a `subOf` register is REFUSED AT CONFIG LOAD (`TargetSchemaData::validate()`), and the cc lists are the only source `allocatable` is built from — so none of these names can reach a register pool.
⚠⚠ THE LOW-BYTE NAMES OF rsp/rbp/rsi/rdi ARE `spl`/`bpl`/`sil`/`dil` AND REQUIRE A REX PREFIX — without one, encoding 4..7 in a byte-register slot names the LEGACY HIGH bytes `ah`/`ch`/`dh`/`bh`, i.e. a DIFFERENT physical register. `setcc`'s template already carries `forceRexPrefix: true` for exactly this reason (D-LIR-SETCC-WIDTH-CONTRACT), so these four are safe there. `ah`/`ch`/`dh`/`bh` are deliberately UNDECLARED: they are not sub-registers of rax..rbx in the `subOf` sense this table means (they alias bits 8..15, not 0..7), and declaring them with the same parent would make the narrow-spelling resolution silently read the wrong byte.

$asmConstraintsComment:
★★★ WHICH GNU INLINE-ASM CONSTRAINT LETTER MEANS WHICH REGISTER IS TARGET VOCABULARY, AND THEREFORE LIVES HERE. `"=a"(o)` means RAX; nothing in the C standard says so, and a C++ table keyed on architecture would be an agnosticism break that no grep catches until arm64 inline asm arrives — at which point the table is load-bearing.
★★ THE LINE AGAINST [[D-CONFIG-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARED-AS-TARGET-VOCABULARY]], WHICH REVERTED AN `asmSyntax` BLOCK ON THIS FILE. That block died because `registerPrefix`/`immediatePrefix`/comment chars/operand order are (target, DIALECT) facts — ✔MEASURED, AT&T `movq %rsi, (%rdi)` vs Intel `mov QWORD PTR [rdi], rsi`, ONE CPU. Constraint letters take the same test and PASS it: `=a` means RAX under AT&T and under Intel, in ELF and in PE. The letter names a REGISTER; a register is a property of the processor. ⇒ no sigils, no operand order, no mnemonic spellings may ever enter this array. The MODIFIERS `= + & %` are GNU-asm grammar owned by the source language and the loader REJECTS a letter containing one.
★ THREE AXES, ALL BOUND TO VOCABULARY THAT ALREADY EXISTED — no fourth axis, no `AsmConstraint*` verb set: `registerClass` → TargetRegClass, `register` → this file's own `registers[].name` (the `implicitRegisters` name-resolution precedent, resolved to an ordinal AT LOAD), `operandKind` → OperandKindFilter, the same closed set the encoding variant guards use.
✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 x86_64, `-O2 -S`, WITH THREE COMPETING LIVE `"r"` OPERANDS so a lucky allocation cannot be mistaken for a pin: r→%rax, a→%rax, b→%rbx, c→%rcx, d→%rdx, S→%rsi, D→%rdi, x→%xmm0; `"m"(*p)`→`(%rdi)`; `"i"(7)`→`$7`. ⚠ CASE IS LOAD-BEARING: `d` is %rdx and `D` is %rdi — two different registers, one letter apart.
★★ `q` IS DECLARED AND `Q` IS NOT, AND THE DIFFERENCE WAS MEASURED AFTER AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS VERY COMMENT ASSERTED IT WRONGLY. That draft grouped `q` with `Q` as 'the byte-addressable subclass' and refused both — asserted from the letter's NAME, never probed. ✔THE PROBE, which counts how many SIMULTANEOUS live operands each letter admits (the register-set size, read off the point where gcc says 'impossible constraints'): **r=15, q=15, Q=4, x=16, a=1**. So on THIS target `q` admits exactly the registers `r` does — REX makes every GPR byte-addressable, so the i386 subclass {a,b,c,d} that the letter's name remembers does not exist here — and `q`→`gpr` is EXACT, not an approximation. `Q`=4 is a genuine subset and stays out. ⚠ The lesson generalizes past this row: a constraint letter's MEANING is per-target, so its register set must be measured per-target and never inferred from what the letter means somewhere else. `a`=1 is the control that shows the probe can see a single-register pin.
⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED: `Q`. ✔MEASURED 4 registers ({rax,rbx,rcx,rdx}); `TargetRegClass` cannot express a SUBSET of a class, and declaring it as plain `gpr` would be a knob that LIES — it would load clean, read as support, and hand the allocator 11 registers gcc forbids. A letter this file cannot describe EXACTLY is a letter it refuses by name.
★ THE DEFERRAL, stated here because it has no registry row yet (the lane that owns .plans must add it, and this sentence is the handover): expressing a register SUBCLASS needs a FOURTH binding axis — an explicit list of register names — which is deliberately NOT built. Trigger: the first client corpus whose inline asm actually uses a subclass letter. ✔MEASURED that none does today — sqlite's src/hwtime.h, the only inline asm in the corpus, uses exactly `"=a"`, `"=d"` and `"=r"`. Building the axis before that trigger fires would be a speculative build with no consumer, so the honest state is: refuse the letter loudly, and let the refusal be the thing that fires when a client needs it.
✔MEASURED `x`→%xmm0, and its register set is **16** by the same simultaneous-operand probe, which is exactly the 16 `fpr` rows this file declares (xmm0-xmm15) ⇒ `x`→`fpr` is EXACT here. ★ THE SAME LETTER IS *NOT* EXACT ON AARCH64 — there `x` measures 16 out of a 32-register V file, i.e. the V0-V15 SUBCLASS — so arm64.target.json refuses it while this file declares it. One letter, two processors, opposite decisions, both measured: that is the facet earning its existence.

asmConstraints.$comment: The general-register class. ✔%rax with three competing "r" operands live — an allocation, not a pin, which is exactly what a CLASS binding means.

★ THE PIN THAT PROVES A CLASS IS NOT ENOUGH: given three competing "r" operands the `"=a"` output STILL landed in %rax. sqlite's own hwtime.h reads the TSC with `"=a"(lo),"=d"(hi)`, which is unencodable without these two rows.
UPPERCASE S and D — the string-instruction source/destination registers. Distinct from lowercase `d` (%rdx) by CASE ALONE; the loader is case-sensitive and a test pins it.

The byte-addressable general registers. ✔MEASURED to admit 15 simultaneous live operands — the SAME count as `r` — because REX makes every GPR byte-addressable on x86_64; the i386 {a,b,c,d} subclass the letter's name remembers does not exist on this target, so `gpr` is EXACT here and not an approximation. Contrast `Q` (4), which is why that one is absent.

Operand FORM, not a register: `m` accepts a memory reference. Bound to `membase` — the HEAD of the (membase, memoffset) pair a LIR memory reference is built from; the displacement rides in the paired memoffset slot and needs no letter of its own. ✔MEASURED `"m"(*p)` → `(%rdi)`. ★ REALIZED END-TO-END, AND THAT SENTENCE IS NEW: the pipeline used to REFUSE this letter with `has no resolved register class — the constraint letter was never bound to a processor`, about the row you are reading. The CST→HIR resolution carried only two of `binds`’ three arms, so a DECLARED form-bound letter was byte-identical to an UNDECLARED one. The ADDRESS is what gets a register; the FORM decides what the template writes around it. (D-ASM-MEMORY-CONSTRAINT-REFUSED-DESPITE-BEING-DECLARED; witnessed by execution in `examples/c-subset/c_inline_asm_memory_operand`.) ★ THE OUTPUT DIRECTION (`"=m"`, `"+m"`, `"=&m"`) IS REALIZED TOO, BY THE SAME CARRIAGE: the operand's ADDRESS in a register, with the direction living entirely inside the template's own instruction (D-ASM-MEMORY-CONSTRAINT-OUTPUT-FORM-NOT-REALIZED; witnessed by execution in `examples/c-subset/c_inline_asm_memory_output_operand`). ⚠ THIS SENTENCE REPLACED ONE THAT SAID THE OPPOSITE and had gone stale one cycle after it was written (*"a different mechanism — no register to capture, no result piece to anchor — and is still refused BY NAME"*); a config comment that reads as evidence is worth exactly as much as its last re-measurement (D-CONFIG-ASM-CONSTRAINT-COMMENT-CLAIMS-A-REFUSAL-THAT-NO-LONGER-EXISTS). ⓘ WHAT THE TEMPLATE MAY SPELL AROUND A MEMORY OPERAND IS A SEPARATE, OPCODE-TABLE QUESTION, and this letter never answered it: the read-modify-write forms `addq $5, %0` / `subq %1, %0` and their memory-SOURCE twins landed 2026-08-23 in this file's `opcodes` array, not here (D-TARGET-X86-64-DECLARES-NO-MEMORY-DESTINATION-ARITHMETIC).

✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -S`: `"i"(7)` → `$7`. `imm32` is the JSON-side historical width label for OperandKindFilter::ImmInt — the SAME spelling the encoding variant guards use, deliberately reused rather than re-minted. ★ REALIZED END-TO-END, AND THAT SENTENCE IS NEW: the pipeline used to REFUSE this letter by name (`binds the operand form 'imm32', which this pipeline does not yet realize`) while this row correctly declared it. An immediate binds NO register — the number is written INTO the instruction — so the VALUE travels instead, as an ordinary MIR `Const`, and the tier that binds it reads the constant back out. (D-ASM-IMMEDIATE-CONSTRAINT-FORM-NOT-REALIZED; witnessed by execution in `examples/c-subset/c_inline_asm_immediate_operand`.) ⚠ THE OPERAND MUST BE AN INTEGER CONSTANT EXPRESSION AND IS PROVEN ONE, NOT ASSUMED: ✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 at -O0 AND -O2, a runtime value here is `error: impossible constraint in 'asm'`, and DSS refuses it too. The accepted set is gcc's — `"i"(1+2)` → `$3`, `"i"(K)` for an enum constant → `$9`, `"i"(sizeof(int))` → `$4` — so folding is required, not optional. An `"=i"` OUTPUT is refused on both sides (gcc: `output number 0 not directly addressable`): a constant is a value, not a location.

$registerClassOpsComment: FC2 Part B: per-register-class move/load/store mnemonics. A class WITHOUT a row uses the universal defaults (mov/load/store) iff it is gpr — the substrate default class; every other row-less class FAILS LOUD at the consumer (a GPR mov against an XMM hwEncoding assembles to valid-looking-but-WRONG bytes — the class-blind silent miscompile this table kills). fpr's `store` landed with its FIRST consumer (trigger discipline honored): the ms_x64 prologue saved-reg spill — Win64 callee-saved xmm6-15 + regalloc's callee-saved-first policy put the first FPR vreg in a callee-saved xmm, and classOpHandle failed loud L_RequiredLirOpcodeMissing until movsd_store was declared.
$callingConventionsComment: Per-platform x86_64 ABIs. ML7 callconv lowering selects one based on driver flag / function attribute. SysV AMD64 = Linux/macOS/BSD; ms_x64 = Windows. argGprs/argFprs ordering is significant (caller MUST place int args in those registers in that order, then spill to stack).

callingConventions.name: sysv_amd64
callingConventions.$comment: System V AMD64 ABI (Linux, macOS, BSD). Integer args: RDI/RSI/RDX/RCX/R8/R9 then stack. Float args: XMM0..7 then stack. Integer return: RAX (low 64 bits) + RDX (high 64 bits if >64-bit aggregate). Float return: XMM0/XMM1. Stack 16-byte aligned BEFORE call (RSP%16==0); the call instruction pushes RIP, leaving RSP%16==8 at callee entry. 128-byte red zone below RSP for leaf functions.
callingConventions.$framePointerComment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): rbp is the frame-pointer register a VLA function reserves as a stable fixed-frame base (captured at the fixed-frame bottom, then every fixed-frame ref switches SP→rbp so it survives the runtime `sub rsp,<vlaSize>`). A NON-VLA function never reserves it — rbp stays an ordinary callee-saved allocatable GPR (byte-identical frames). Consumed by lir_regalloc (pool exclusion) + lir_callconv (force-save + prologue capture + epilogue restore).
callingConventions.$aggregateAbiComment: FC7 (D-FC7-STRUCT-BY-VALUE-ARG-RETURN): System V AMD64 §3.2.3 eightbyte classification — a struct/union ≤16 bytes is passed/returned in up to two registers (each 8-byte 'eightbyte' classified INTEGER→GPR or SSE→FPR per the field types overlapping it); larger than aggregateMaxRegBytes (16) goes in MEMORY (by-reference args / sret returns). No indirectResultRegister ⇒ the sret hidden pointer is a first INTEGER arg (rdi) returned in rax (vs AAPCS64's x8). The classification ALGORITHM lives in the aggregate_abi realization tier keyed on this strategy enum, never on cc.name/target identity.
callingConventions.$aggregateStackExhaustsComment: D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS: System V §3.2.3 — when a by-value aggregate does not fit the remaining arg registers, 'the assignments get reverted' and it is passed wholly on the stack, but the leftover registers REMAIN AVAILABLE for a later (smaller) arg (gcc function_arg_advance_64 leaves cum->nregs untouched). false = BACKFILL — the per-class cursor is NOT advanced. This DIVERGES from AAPCS64 (true/exhaust); declared explicitly so the fact is visible in config, not buried in a default.
callingConventions.$entryStackPointerBiasComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-TRAMP-PROLOGUE: at SysV process entry the kernel maps the image and JUMPS to `_start` with RSP 16-byte-aligned and NO return address pushed — so RSP bias mod stackAlignment is 0. The trampoline emitter computes its prologue `sub rsp, N` via `alignedSizeWithBias(shadowSpaceBytes=0, stackAlignment=16, bias=0) = 0` — no prologue emitted, which is correct for SysV (no shadow space + already aligned).
callingConventions.$callPushBytesComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-ML7-FRAME-BIAS-UNIFY: x86_64 `call` instruction pushes the 8-byte return address. ML7 `computeFrameLayout` consumes this as the bias for non-leaf functions so their prologue `sub rsp, N` produces RSP ≡ 0 mod 16 at the next call site. SysV's entry bias is 0 (kernel JMP) but this in-program call-push is 8 — the two distinct facts coincide on Win64 (both 8) and diverge here. Without this wired, the user-fn → extern-call shadow-space + alignment violation reappears one stack frame below the trampoline (the same 0xC0000005 class as D-LK10-ENTRY-TRAMP-PROLOGUE, now recurring at the user-fn boundary).
callingConventions.$variadicVectorCountRegComment: D-LANG-VARIADIC (step 13.4, 2026-06-02): SysV AMD64 §3.5.7 — the caller MUST set AL to the number of vector (XMM) registers used to pass variadic arguments before any call to a function with `...`. printf reads %al to know whether to consult the XMM save area in its va_list walk; passing AL uninitialized yields garbage formatting and (on hardened glibcs) an abort. C-subset has no float type today, so every variadic call from c-subset stamps the count as 0; the count-of-FPRs logic in ML7 materialize is data-driven via this field — future float support (in c-subset or any other source language) lights up the same code path with zero substrate change. The field names `rax` (the register table's canonical full-width name) rather than `al` (the ABI document's low-byte alias) because the register table does NOT yet model the x86 subregister aliases (al / ax / eax for the low-byte / low-word / low-dword of rax); anchored D-TARGET-SUBREGISTER-ALIASES. Writing rax = count is ABI-equivalent: a `mov rax, <count<=8>` sets AL to the same byte and the upper bits are irrelevant to printf's ABI contract.
callingConventions.$vaListLayoutComment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): System V AMD64 §3.5.7 variadic-CALLEE layout. `__va_list_tag` = {u32 gp_offset@0; u32 fp_offset@4; void* overflow_arg_area@8; void* reg_save_area@16;} = 24B. A variadic callee's prologue spills the 6 integer arg regs (rdi..r9, 8B each = 48B) then the al-gated 8 SSE arg regs (xmm0..xmm7, 16B each = 128B) into a 176B register-save-area. va_start sets gp_offset = fixedGPR*8, fp_offset = 48 + fixedSSE*16, reg_save_area = &save, overflow_arg_area = &(incoming stack args). va_arg(T) of an INTEGER reads reg_save_area+gp_offset (bump +8) while gp_offset < gpOffsetLimit(48), else overflow; an SSE arg reads reg_save_area+fp_offset (bump +16) while fp_offset < fpOffsetLimit(176), else overflow. Every fact is config — the HIR→MIR diamond + LIR prologue spill read these, never branching on cc.name/arch/format. ★ STALENESS FIXED 2026-07-25: this note used to end "Win64/AAPCS64 omit this block (different variadic ABI) and fail loud at the va_start site" — no longer true, and it had become actively misleading. Every shipped CC now declares its own `vaListLayout`, each naming a DIFFERENT `strategy`: `ms_x64` two rows below (homogeneous_pointer, FC12b), arm64 `aapcs64` (aapcs64_dual_cursor, FC12c) and `apple_arm64` (homogeneous_pointer). So the block is not a SysV-only opt-in whose absence means fail-loud; it is the per-CC declaration of WHICH variadic model applies, and `strategy` is the closed-vocabulary verb the engine dispatches on. Absent `vaListLayout` now describes only a hypothetical future CC that declares none — nothing shipped.

callingConventions.name: ms_x64
callingConventions.$comment: Microsoft x64 ABI (Windows). First 4 args in RCX/RDX/R8/R9 regardless of int-vs-float (slot-aligned: an XMM arg in slot N uses XMM_N AND consumes the matching GPR slot, even if the GPR is unused; symmetrically, an integer in slot N consumes XMM_N). Integer return: RAX. Float return: XMM0. Stack 16-byte aligned before call; 32-byte shadow space (home space) always allocated by caller for callee to spill arg registers. No red zone.
callingConventions.$aggregateComment: FC7 C2 (D-FC7-STRUCT-BY-VALUE-ARG-RETURN): MS x64 by-value aggregates. A struct/union of size 1/2/4/8 (power of two ≤ 8) is passed/returned in ONE GPR (treated as an integer of its size — Win64 has no SSE/HFA rule); every other size (3/5/6/7 or > 8) goes BY REFERENCE: a caller-allocated copy for args, an sret hidden pointer (in RCX, arg slot 0) returning the pointer in RAX for results. `win64_by_size` drives the bounded `classifyAggregate` arm; maxRegBytes = 8 (a single register).
callingConventions.$framePointerComment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): rbp is the frame-pointer register a VLA function reserves as a stable fixed-frame base (captured at the fixed-frame bottom, then every fixed-frame ref switches SP→rbp so it survives the runtime `sub rsp,<vlaSize>`). A NON-VLA function never reserves it — rbp stays an ordinary callee-saved allocatable GPR (byte-identical frames). Consumed by lir_regalloc (pool exclusion) + lir_callconv (force-save + prologue capture + epilogue restore).
callingConventions.$entryStackPointerBiasComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-TRAMP-PROLOGUE: at Windows process entry, `RtlUserThreadStart` does a CALL into the entry point, so RSP at the first trampoline instruction is ≡8 mod 16. The trampoline emitter computes its prologue `sub rsp, N` via `alignedSizeWithBias(shadowSpaceBytes=32, stackAlignment=16, bias=8)`: smallest N >= 32 with N ≡ 8 mod 16 = 40. That single `sub rsp, 0x28` (a) reserves 32 bytes of caller-side shadow space for ExitProcess + (b) realigns RSP from ≡8 to ≡0 mod 16 so both `call user_entry` and `call [iat_ExitProcess]` enter their callees at the ABI-mandated RSP ≡8 mod 16. Without this field wired, ExitProcess's aligned-SSE stores produced STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION on CLI-emitted binaries (smoke test `mov eax,42; ret` hid it because the test fn never touched the stack and the specific ExitProcess code path didn't hit movaps with misaligned RSP).
callingConventions.$callPushBytesComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-ML7-FRAME-BIAS-UNIFY: x86_64 `call` instruction pushes the 8-byte return address (same as SysV — ISA-level fact). ML7 `computeFrameLayout` for any non-leaf Win64 function emits `sub rsp, N` where N satisfies BOTH N >= max(savedRegs+spill, shadowSpaceBytes=32) AND N ≡ callPushBytes=8 (mod stackAlignment=16) — same `alignedSizeWithBias` helper the trampoline emitter uses. For a hello_puts-shape main (no callee-saved, no spills, calls puts): raw = max(0, 32) = 32; N = alignedSizeWithBias(32, 16, 8) = 40. Main's prologue becomes `sub rsp, 0x28`; main calls puts at RSP ≡ 0 mod 16 (Win64 ABI requirement) with 32 bytes of shadow space available for puts's register-arg home area. This closes the actual cause of the 2026-06-02 hello_puts SEGV — NOT a CRT-init gap (msvcrt's DllMain self-inits stdio at DLL load).
callingConventions.$stackProbePageBytesComment: D-WIN64-LARGE-FRAME-STACK-PROBE: the Windows x86-64 stack guard-page size (4096). A function whose total frame EXCEEDS 4096 bytes must touch every page on the way down (committing each PAGE_GUARD page) instead of a bare `sub rsp, F` that jumps over the guard page → STATUS_GUARD_PAGE_VIOLATION → access violation on the first deep write. The ML7 prologue reads this generically and, when totalFrameSize > 4096, emits the `stack_probe` virtual op (page step = this value) which the x86_64 encoder lowers to an inline page-walking loop — INSTEAD of the plain `sub rsp, F`. NO __chkstk dependency (dss PE exes are freestanding; __chkstk lives in msvcrt/ucrt). sysv_amd64 omits this field (0 = no probing: Linux auto-grows the stack via demand paging). Agnostic: the prologue branches on the VALUE, never on cc.name/arch/format.
callingConventions.$slotAlignedComment: D-ML7-2.6 (closed co-with-D-ML7-2.2, 2026-06-02): Win64 ms_x64 uses SLOT-ALIGNED arg passing — each arg consumes one shared slot index regardless of register class. Slot N reserves BOTH argGprs[N] AND argFprs[N]. `f(int, double, int, double, int)` consumes slots 0..4 → (rcx OR xmm0, rdx OR xmm1, r8 OR xmm2, r9 OR xmm3, [rsp+0x20]). Pure-GPR calls (WriteFile, GetStdHandle, etc.) happen to give the same overflow count as independent counters; mixed-class calls require the slot-aligned counting to land arg-5 on the stack correctly. ML7 `computeMaxOutgoingStackArgs` + `materializeOneFunc` consult this flag.
callingConventions.$vaListLayoutComment: FC12b (D-FC12B-WIN64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): Microsoft x64 variadic-CALLEE layout. `va_list` is a plain `char*` (sizeof 8) — the HomogeneousPointer strategy, NOT SysV's __va_list_tag/register-save-area. Win64 spills the first 4 named integer args into the caller-provided 32-byte HOME SPACE (rcx/rdx/r8/r9 slots) which sits CONTIGUOUS with the 5th+ stack args, so `va_arg` is a LINEAR pointer bump by namedArgSlotBytes (8) across home→overflow — no diamond, no per-class cursor. The callee prologue spills the named integer arg regs into their home slots; `va_start` sets ap = &home[namedArgCount]. FP varargs are passed in BOTH the XMM and matching integer register, and the callee reads va_arg(double) from the home (GPR) slot — so the CALLER duplicates each FP vararg into the matching integer reg (lir_callconv, strategy-gated). Struct-by-value varargs are DEFERRED this cycle (D-FC12B-WIN64-STRUCT-VARARG, fail-loud). Every fact is config — the lowering + spill read these, never branching on cc.name/arch/format.

$condCodeEncodingComment: D-CSUBSET-WHILE-LOOP-SUBSTRATE (step 13.5 cycle 1, 2026-06-03): per-cond-code nibble mapping for x86 setcc / jcc opcodes. The encoder OR's this nibble into the LOW 4 BITS of the LAST opcode byte: setcc emits `0F 9x` (where x = cc nibble); jcc emits `0F 8x rel32`. Numeric values from Intel SDM Vol. 1 Appendix B (condition code encoding table). The 10 integer arms are REQUIRED; the FC3.5 float arms (next comment) are per-entry optional. ARM64 declares its own table mapping into bits 0..3 of the B.cc instruction word — different numeric values, same field-position abstraction (D-AS3-COND-CODE-ARM64 anchor).
$condCodeEncodingFloatComment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (FCmp lowering — D-COND-FLOAT-NAN-TRUTHINESS-FCMP): float condition arms over the UCOMISD/UCOMISS flag truth table (Intel SDM: unordered → ZF=PF=CF=1; greater → all 0; less → CF=1; equal → ZF=1). fogt = `a` (CF=0∧ZF=0, nibble 7 — false on unordered); foge = `ae` (CF=0, nibble 3); fone = `ne` (ZF=0, nibble 5 — false on BOTH equal and unordered, so plain setne IS ordered-ne on x86); fuo = `p` (PF=1, nibble 0xA — after UCOMI the parity flag IS the unordered predicate); ford = `np` (nibble 0xB). foeq/fune are deliberately ABSENT: sete is TRUE on unordered (ZF conflation) — no single x86 cc realizes them; their absence signals the MIR→LIR composed realization (Oeq = sete∧setnp, Une = setne∨setp). Olt/Ole need no entries — the lowering swap-canonicalizes them to fogt/foge.
$relocationsComment: Relocation taxonomy (plan 13 AS4 + plan 14 LK6 cycle 1 + D-LK6-1 closure 2026-06-01). Opaque uint32 `kind` tags the assembler stamps onto each emitted Relocation; the linker reads via TargetSchema::relocationInfo(kind). `formula` is a CLOSED-ENUM DISCRIMINATOR (load-bearing — see RelocFormulaKind in target_schema.hpp): 'linear' (S + A + (pcRel ? -P : 0) + addendBias; widthBytes LE), or one of the bit-shift variants ('aarch64_call26' / 'aarch64_adr_prel_pg_hi21' / 'aarch64_add_abs_lo12'). For 'linear', the structured fields (pcRelative + addendBias + widthBytes) parameterize the formula. Tag values are arbitrary per-target — only the NAME round-trips with format.json cross-reference.

relocations.$comment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the local-exec thread-pointer-offset patch — value = S + A, written 4 LE bytes, where S is the SIGNED tpoff the walker bit-casts into symbolVa[sym] (Variant II: templateOffset − alignedBlockSize, negative) — the SAME Linear formula as abs32, ZERO new RelocFormulaKind. `tls: true` marks the kind thread-local-offset-bearing for the walker's TLS symbol ⟺ tls-kind cross-check (a non-TLS reloc against a TLS symbol would write the bit-cast tpoff as a VA — the CRIT-1 garbage-pointer class; a tls reloc against a non-TLS symbol would write a VA as a tpoff). Emitted by the 2-op [reg, symbol] `lea` variant at the memory-displacement position (memreloc.disp32).

relocations.$comment: D-UNWIND-NO-EH-FRAME-IN-RELOCATABLE-OBJECTS: a 32-bit PC-relative reference with NO implicit bias — the DWARF FDE `initial_location` field in a relocatable `.eh_frame` (DW_EH_PE_pcrel|sdata4). It is a DATA field, not an instruction operand, so the -4 that makes `rel32` correct for a call site (whose displacement is relative to the instruction END) would make this one point 4 bytes past its function. The two kinds emit the SAME ELF wire type (R_X86_64_PC32 = 2) and differ ONLY in the psABI implicit addend, which is exactly why they must be two rows: the bias is a property of the PATCH SITE and this schema is where a patch site's bias is declared. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 against `gcc -c`: `readelf -r` shows `R_X86_64_PC32  .text + 0` on the first FDE — addend = the function's offset within .text, bias 0.
